oeis-a243928.note: Kimberling's 2014 conjecture that x -> x+1, x -> -3/x generate every rational from 1. Uniqueness is automatic from first-occurrence rows. The proof shows closure under x -> x-1 through a positive word in the two maps, with five exceptional points handled separately, and then a Euclidean descent. A short but genuine argument; no prior proof found (A243929/A243925 still list it as a conjecture).

oeis-a248231.note: Oudra's formula for the least k with zeta(5)-H_k^(5) < 1/n^4. Tail bounds around 1/(4(k+1/2)^4) plus the parity gap between (2k+1)^2 (odd) and 2n^2-4 (even) settle every n. Checked numerically for n < 60. Elementary analytic estimate; routine.

oeis-a256132.note: Sun's 2015 conjecture: every n is w(3w+1)/2 + three pentagonal numbers x(3x-1)/2 (w,x,y,z >= 0). The proof combines Gauss-Legendre three squares (adapted from Kitamura's Lean development) with residue and centre selection and a finite check below 5000. No published proof found (Krachun-Sun 2020 and Ju 2020 treat other coefficient patterns; the entry still says conjecture). Moderately substantive.

oeis-a260619.note: The arithmetic derivative of the hyperfactorial equals H(n)*sum_{i<=n} i': induction with the Leibniz rule (k^k)' = k^k * k * k'/k. Routine.

oeis-a265716.note: McEachen's bitwise formula for n IMPL 2n is a direct bit identity. Routine.

oeis-a281648.note: Manyama's 'iff n = 6, 10 or a power of 2' (checked to 1024; the b-file to 1000 has no counterexample) is false at n = 3330: num(B_6660) mod 3330 = 3329. This is certified via von Staudt-Clausen modulo 2, 5 and 37 and a 3-adic Faulhaber bound modulo 9. No prior counterexample found. It is a computational counterexample, so routine.

oeis-a289873.note: Barker's rational g.f. for the quasi-polynomial (n^2-(n mod 6 - 3)^2)/3. Routine.

oeis-a302706.note: Cicuttin's limit a(n)/(2n) -> 1 with near-n maximizers. Since x^2+y^2 == 2x^2 mod (x+y), an explicit choice gives remainders 2n - o(n), and remainder < x+y forces both coordinates ~ n. Elementary.

oeis-a318291.note: Musatov's conjecture: for each odd prime p, infinitely many j (p not dividing j) with j*2^k - p composite for all k > 0. The proof uses covering systems (two certificates, so one avoids p) and CRT families j = pR + Q(ps+1). It extends Israel's p=3 covering in the entry. This is a standard Riesel-type covering argument; routine for the area.

oeis-a327836.note: Since n == -1 mod n+1, lifting the exponent gives n^(2(n+1)^n) == 1 mod (n+1)^(n+1), so the order divides 2(n+1)^n. Routine.

oeis-a330715.note: Barker's linear recurrence and quasi-polynomial for a mod-recursion that becomes eventually regular (definition matches data). Routine.

oeis-a337868.note: Greathouse's characterization a(n) = phi(n)+1 iff n is p or p^2: any other n has a nonzero non-unit power residue such as p^2 mod p^3 or p^r mod pq (definition matches data). Elementary.

oeis-a345211.note: Eldar's conjecture that the terms are even and their halves are exactly the m not in A157932. A157932 is a periodic residue condition, and the refactorable-divisor counts are compared via the 2-adic part. Elementary characterization; routine.

oeis-a383246.note: Xausa's conjecture that A342043 sorted equals A383246. The statement models A342043's greedy rule with a local admissibility test, justified because repunits always continue the sequence, so no dead ends. The proof shows every admissible number is eventually chosen. Routine.

oeis-a387064.note: Wu's a(p^k) = (p-1)p^(k-1): by Kummer, rows below p^k have v_p <= k-1, and in row p^k exactly the C(p^k,j) with p not dividing j are divisible by p^k. Routine.

oeis-a071622.note: The statement matches Cloitre's conjecture: a(n) = -Sum (-1)^floor((4/3)^k), and for n > 2300, a(n) > log(n)^2. The disproof exhibits a(18966)=0 by kernel computation. A Python check confirms the first violation already at n=16954 (a=94 < log^2 n = 94.83) and a(18966)=0. I found no earlier report of a counterexample. This is a finite computation.

oeis-a002660.note: Irvine's 2014 conjecture: a(n) is the inverse Moebius transform of the series with g.f. (x+2x^2+2x^3-2x^4)/(1-x)^2. That series has coefficients b(d)=d^2 for d<=3 and 3d for d>=4, so the sum of b(d) over divisors d of n is exactly the defining sum. The formal statement over Q[[x]] is faithful. The OEIS entry still says 'Conjectured'. It is immediate from the definition.

oeis-a024469.note: This is Mathar's 2020 g.f. conjecture, stated with the denominator cleared. The common sign flip is correct: (x^2-x-1)=-(1+x-x^2) and (x^2+x-1)^2=(1-x-x^2)^2. The definition of a(n) as the sum of L(k)L(n+1-k) for k=1..floor((n+1)/2), with Lucas L(0)=2, L(1)=1, reproduces 1,3,13,19,48. This is a routine rational g.f. identity, still marked as a conjecture in the entry.

oeis-a028841.note: Barker's g.f. and the recurrence a(n)=a(n-1)+a(n-5)-a(n-6). The iterated digit sum is the digital root, so membership depends only on n mod 9 (roots 1,2,3,5,8), which gives a(n+5)=a(n)+9. The formalization (digital root, Fibonacci test via Nat.fib, offset 1) is faithful. This is a routine periodicity / g.f. identity.

oeis-a047239.note: Kimberling's greedy characterization of the numbers that are 1 or 2 mod 6. Sums of three such numbers are 3, 4, 5 or 0 mod 6, and every number in a gap is such a sum (3=1+1+1, ..., 6=2+2+2, and so on). The formal IsLeast statement, which uses the closed form for earlier terms and allows k=n, is equivalent to the greedy property by induction. Routine.

oeis-a092506.note: Cloitre's conjecture: phi(x)+phi(x-1)=floor((3x-2)/2) exactly for the primes 2^n+1. For odd x the left side is at most (x-1)+(x-1)/2, with equality iff x is prime and x-1 is a power of 2. For even x>2 it is at most x/2+x-2, which is too small, and x=2 is a solution. The set equality is faithful (x=1 excluded correctly). Elementary totient bounds.

oeis-a110515.note: Barry's formula T(n,k)=Jacobi(2^(n-k),2(n-k)+1). The coefficients of (1-x+x^2+x^3)/(1-x^4) are periodic (1,-1,1,1). Jacobi(2,2m+1)^m has the same period-4 pattern, by the supplementary law for (2/q). The formalization is faithful. Routine.

oeis-a112703.note: This is Mathar's 2016 recurrence (n+1)a(n)+(-37n+17)a(n-1)+18(2n-1)a(n-2)=0 for partial sums of 9^k Catalan(k). It follows from (k+2)C(k+1)=2(2k+1)C(k). The formal statement is faithful. Routine P-recursive identity.

oeis-a131935.note: These are Barker's 2018 recurrence and g.f. for the Khalimsky-continuous function counts. The sequence is defined through Samieinia's endpoint recurrences, which reproduce 4, 7, 15, ... Sloane's note in the entry says it 'should be straightforward to prove'. It is a routine linear-recurrence consequence of the given transfer recurrences.

oeis-a157218.note: Sun's 2009 conjecture says every odd m>34 is p+2^x+7*2^y, with p prime = 1 mod 6 and x,y>=1. The formal statement matches the 'in other words' form exactly. The disproof certifies that m=445466268731 has no representation. An independent Python check (Miller-Rabin over all x,y) confirms 0 representations, and the same code reproduces the OEIS data. The conjecture had only been verified to 1.5e8, and I found no earlier counterexample. It is a finite computational counterexample.

oeis-a173644.note: Seidov's recurrence a(n)=2a(n-7)-a(n-14) for the least m>0 with n^2+7m a square. The proof uses the closed form 7a(n)=d(2n+d), where d is the least d>=1 with 7 | 2n+d, which is quasi-polynomial with period 7. The formal statement for n>=15 is faithful and reproduces 5,3,1,12,8,4,21. Routine.

oeis-a178296.note: Mathar's closed form a(n)=10^n/2+2*8^n-5*6^n/2 for collinear 5-point subsets of {0..5}^n. The formal count uses real collinearity of 5-element sets, which matches a(1)=6, a(2)=88, a(3)=984. The proof is an explicit double count of step-4/step-5 parameterizations. It is an elementary lattice-line counting identity, still marked as a conjecture in the entry.

oeis-a181069.note: Bala's Aug 2026 supercongruence: a(n p^k) = a(n p^(k-1)) mod p^(3k) for all primes p>=5, where a(n)=Sum C(n-1,k)^3 C(n,k). This formula follows from the l.g.f. by reindexing (I checked a(2)=3, a(3)=28). The formal statement is faithful. The 2155-line proof adapts the Osburn-Sahu-Straub reciprocal-square method and the Robert-Zuber valuation bound. I found no earlier proof (Kallat's 2026 papers do not cover A181069). A substantive supercongruence.

oeis-a187029.note: These are Barker's g.f. and third-difference recurrence for Hardin's 4-square queen tours, with moves of 1 or 2 squares. A Python re-implementation of the formal 'term' reproduces the data 0, 24, 1344, 7056, ... exactly, and the (1-x)^3 numerator matches. The count is eventually quadratic because each tour's bounding box is at most 6x6. Routine.

oeis-a192466.note: Barker's closed form (-1-(-1)^n+2^n+4^n)/3 and order-4 recurrence for the x-coefficient of 1+x^n+x^(2n) mod x^2-x-2. Evaluating the remainder at the roots 2 and -1 gives the formula at once. Faithful formalization (remainder modulo the monic polynomial). Routine.

oeis-a192939.note: This is Mathar's 2014 recurrence a(n)+(1-4n)a(n-1)+(4n^2-6n+1)a(n-2)=0, for the constant term of (x+2)...(x+2n) mod x^2-x-1. The formal statement is faithful (it matches 1, 2, 9, 61). Routine linear-algebra recurrence in the basis {1,x}.

oeis-a203165.note: This is Mathar's g.f. and recurrence a(n)=48a(n-4)-576a(n-8) for the (n-1)st elementary symmetric function of 3,4,1,2,3,4,... Each period multiplies the product by 24 and adds 50 times it to e_{n-1}, which gives the recurrence. The formalization, with a(0)=0 adjoined, is faithful. Routine.

oeis-a210529.note: The conjecture is that a(n) exists for all n: 1 or a prime q != p with q^2 = p^2 mod every prime r < sqrt(p). By Dirichlet's theorem there is a prime q = p mod (p-1)!, and that prime is a candidate, so the least candidate exists. The formal candidate set (including q != p, taken from the PARI program) is faithful. Immediate from Dirichlet.

oeis-a223299.note: Barker's recurrence, g.f. and closed form for Hardin's n x 2 graph-coloring arrays. A Python transfer-matrix check of the formal definition gives 36, 324, 3132, ..., matching the data, and the closed form matches. It is a routine transfer-matrix / linear recurrence identity.

oeis-a230089.note: Barker's closed form with powers of i, and the g.f., for the sequence 4 / 2 / n by divisibility. Both depend only on n mod 4 plus a linear term. The formalization is faithful (complex identity for n>=1, cross-multiplied g.f.). Trivial.

oeis-a248520.note: Kotesovec's asymptotic a(n) ~ pi n/(pi-2), for k with floor(cot(pi/(2k+2))) = floor(cot(pi/(2k))). Consecutive cotangent values differ by about 2/pi < 1, so the floors rise by 0 or 1, and the repeats have density 1-2/pi. The formal Tendsto statement (zero-based Nat.nth, ratio to j+1) is faithful. Elementary asymptotics.

oeis-a256480.note: Wu's conjecture (also Conjecture 3 of arXiv:1503.08883): for n odd and not divisible by 5, some repdigit d...d followed by n is prime. Verified up to 1e7. The disproof builds a 96-digit n0 ending in 1 by a covering system. For every digit d and every length k, one of 27 primes dividing R(240) divides d*R(k)*10^96+n0. I re-checked the covering in Python for all d and k<=240 and the period 10^240=1 mod each prime. Wu's paper gives this covering test but conjectured that no such n exists, and I found no earlier counterexample. This is a genuine constructive disproof of a published conjecture.

oeis-a261682.note: Mathar's order-4 P-recursive recurrence for a(n)=2^n+(1+(n mod 2)/2)C(n+1,floor((n+n mod 2)/2))-1. The formal statement over Q for n>=4 is faithful. The proof splits by parity and uses the central binomial ratio. Routine holonomic identity.

oeis-a273400.note: Puszkarz's conjecture: only finitely many n have fewer decimal digits in C(C(C(n))) than C(n). The number of digits of C(C(C(n))) is about 0.6*C(C(n)), which dwarfs C(n). The formal statement (Finite set) is faithful. Trivial growth estimate.

oeis-a294089.note: Sun's conjecture is a conjunction: s(n)*sqrt(5)/pi^(2n) is rational (classical, and proved in the file), and a(n) is a nonzero integer for all n. The formalization follows the entry's definition of b(n) exactly. The disproof shows b(6)=3142014330/691, not an integer, so a(6)=0. An independent exact computation via generalized Bernoulli numbers confirms b(1..5)=1, 2, 1407, 1444, 4540261 and b(6)=3142014330/691. The entry's data stops at n=5 because Mathematica could not evaluate further. A finite Bernoulli-number computation.

oeis-a318807.note: Lagneau's conjecture: when both the squarefree and nonsquarefree divisor sums are squares and their ratio r is an integer, r is a prime square. The merged proof uses w=4963023000=2^3*3^2*5^3*13^3*251. Python confirms s=504^2, sigma-s=135072^2 and r=268^2 with 268 composite. The formal statement matches the entry's subsequence definition. It is a finite counterexample.

oeis-a327978.note: Corneth and Karttunen conjectured that no term (n with n' a primorial > 1) is divisible by 5, and that 9 is the only multiple of 3. The disproof gives n=5^2*307*4227063435109=32442711864461575 with Lucas primality certificates. Python confirms n' = 2*3*5*...*43 exactly. The arithmetic-derivative definition (sum of n/p over prime factors with multiplicity) is faithful. It is a finite counterexample with no earlier report found.

oeis-a330904.note: Koenig's conjecture: no five consecutive integers have equal binary weight and balanced-ternary digit sum. The balanced-ternary digit sum is n mod 2, so a match forces the Thue-Morse bit t(n) to equal n mod 2. For 5 consecutive n that forces t(m)=t(m+1)=t(m+2)=0, which is impossible in Thue-Morse. The formal balanced-ternary recursion is correct. This is an elementary parity argument.

oeis-a337949.note: Hanna's three mod-3 congruences for 2^(n(n-1)/2)+2^(n(n+1)/2). Since 2^k mod 3 depends on the parity of k, and the parities of the triangular exponents are periodic mod 4, this is a finite residue check. Faithful formalization. Trivial.

oeis-a383248.note: Xausa's conjecture: A342044 (greedy digit-stream sequence) is a permutation of A383248 (no digit 9, every non-final odd digit followed by a larger digit). A Python run of the formal 'next/state' model reproduces the first 3000 terms of Sigrist's A342044 b-file exactly, so the encoding is faithful. The proof uses the repdigit 88...8 as a universal bridge, a standard greedy-permutation argument. Routine.

oeis-a003592.note: Sun's 2023 conjecture: every positive n other than 1, 4 and 12 is a sum of distinct numbers 2^a*5^b+1 with none dividing another. Sun verified it only up to 3700. The formal statement (a Finset of such numbers, pairwise non-dividing, summing to n) is faithful, since equal summands would divide each other. The Lean proof combines a kernel-checked initial range with an inductive dyadic-scale balancing construction. I found no earlier proof. This is a genuine Erdos-type representation theorem.

oeis-a036447.note: Kotesovec's 2020 conjecture: a(n)^(1/n) -> sqrt(10) for the double-and-reverse sequence. The proof finds a period-4 'shape' invariant on the leading two digits and the trailing digits (a(4j+6) has a fixed shape). From that, the digit count grows by exactly 2 every 4 steps, which gives 10^(n/2+O(1)). The formal statement is faithful. It is an elementary digit-pattern invariant, so I count it as routine, though it is not a pure formula check.

oeis-a051756.note: Healy's 2024 conjecture: the maximum number of queens on an n x n board each attacking exactly 3 others is 2*floor((6n-2)/5), verified to n=100. McCranie's upper bound was already in the entry. The formal 'visible' (nearest queen on each side of each line, i.e. blocked attacks) matches the data: brute force gives 4, 6, 8 for n=2..4 under blocking, versus 4, 4, 6 without blocking. The proof adds explicit constructions for every residue mod 5. I found no prior proof; the 2026 Ago-Basic-Ciganovic paper treats only the 'at most / exactly one' variant. Substantive extremal combinatorics.

oeis-a347748.note: Spezia's 2021 conjecture: lim a(n)/a(n-1) = 10, where a(n) counts n-digit m that are both (..4)(..4) and (..6)(..6). Such m are 4k with k = 4 mod 5 having divisors in both classes 2 and 3 mod 5. The exceptional k, essentially those built from primes = +-1 mod 5, have density 0, so the count is about c*9*10^(n-1). The proof gets that density-zero step from the divergence of sum 1/p over primes in residue classes mod 10. The formal statement (exact divisor pairs, n-digit window, real ratio limit) is faithful. A modest but genuine analytic density argument; no earlier proof found.

mo-195959.note: Kimberling's 2015 question: for Archimedean copulas with completely monotone f (f(0)=1, f->0, continuous), is C(a,a)-a^2 >= C(u,v)-uv with a=(u+v)/2? The MO answers only handle Clayton cases. The formalization (C^infinity complete monotonicity on (0,inf), invFunOn inverse, C=0 on the axes) is a careful faithful reading. The proof uses Bernstein's theorem to write C(u,v)-uv as a covariance and C(a,a)-a^2 as a variance of exponentials, compared by a Karlin-Novikoff single-crossing argument. A Palomar registry entry for this result is dated 27 Nov 21:50 UTC, after the PR merged (18:59 UTC), so it is not prior work. Substantive.

mo-465929.note: Zolotov's 2024 question has no answers: is there a dimension-free C with W2 <= C*W1 for all pairs of centered Gaussians? The formal statement (Euclidean R^d, couplings as measures with given marginals, Mathlib IsGaussian including singular laws, a single C for all d) is faithful. The costs are finite for Gaussian marginals, so the Bochner integral does not truncate. The proof gives the sharp constant sqrt(pi/2) by aligning covariance factors and testing with weighted sums of |x_i|. I found only one-dimensional or dimension-dependent bounds in the literature. A short but genuine positive answer; moderate confidence that it is not folklore.

oeis-a336279.note: The statement is faithful: a(n) = sum_{k<=n} mu(k) k^5 is positive and negative for arbitrarily large n, which is the entry's unlabelled-author conjecture 'changes sign infinitely often'. It is still listed as a conjecture, and I found no published treatment of these power-weighted Mertens sums. The proof is a genuine analytic argument: a Landau-type oscillation theorem for 1/zeta(s-5), with nonvanishing of zeta on [0,2] minus {1}. The technique is classical (as for M(x)), but it is a real proof, not a finite check.

oeis-a336277.note: This is the same situation as A336279, with k^3 in place of k^5. The statement faithfully encodes 'a(n) changes sign infinitely often' as positive and negative values for arbitrarily large n. It is unmarked in the entry, and I found no earlier proof. The proof is a Landau-oscillation argument for the Mellin transform of the partial sums, using 1/zeta(s-3) and zeta's nonvanishing on [0,2] minus {1}: classical technique, substantive formalization.

mse-1373123.note: The statement transcribes Reshetnikov's PSLQ-discovered Li4 identity (coefficients, arguments, alpha = ln 2, beta = ln 3) exactly, with Li4 as the power series on (0,1). The MSE question has only one speculative answer (score 3, not a proof). The MO repost 261408 got an accepted answer only for the Li5 golden-ratio ladders, not this Li4 identity, and I found no published proof. The 1750-line proof derives a 19-term one-variable functional equation family on [0,1/3] via weight-2/3/4 derivative identities. Substantive.

oeis-a022894.note: Kotesovec's 2019 conjecture lim a(n)^(1/n) = 4 is stated faithfully. a(n) counts sign vectors c(2..2n+1) with 2 + sum c_i p_i = 0, and the offset and prime indexing are correct. It is still labelled a conjecture, and I found no earlier proof. The proof is an elementary but genuine argument: reserve a sublinear set of small odd primes that realise every even correction, flip-prefix injection, Bertrand plus Chebyshev, against the trivial upper bound 4^n.

mo-455020.note: The statement models the PARI loop exactly. A mirror pair gets x+g+gcd(x+g,y+g), the centre gets 3x (A = gcd(x,x) added twice), and v(i) = m(i+1)-2 with m odd >= 3 so entries are positive. It claims (twins => passes) and (eventually passes <=> twins), which are the asker's two conjectures. The question has 0 answers and no settling comments. The proof is a short elementary sieve observation (a mirror pair passes iff both sums are coprime to it; for n >= m+3 a composite candidate has a factor met by the progression).

oeis-a022027.note: Barker's 2015 conjectured recurrence a(n) = 8a(n-1) - 4a(n-3) and g.f. (2-x^2)/(1-8x+4x^3) are stated faithfully, with the greedy rule written as Hasler's ceiling(a(n+1)^2/a(n)) - 1, which is equivalent for positive terms. The entry still labels them conjectures (sequences of this T(a,b) type sometimes break such recurrences, so it was not vacuous). Routine: an invariant 0 < b(n+1)^2 - b(n)b(n+2) <= b(n), proved by induction.

oeis-a200002.note: Kotesovec's 2014 conjecture lim a(n)^(1/n^2) = 4 is stated faithfully. a(n) is written as the coefficient of exp(sum L_r x^r) through a sum over compositions with 1/k!, where L_r = C(2r,r)^r/(2^r r). It is still labelled a conjecture. Routine: the single-block term gives the lower bound and sum of squared block sizes <= n^2 gives the upper bound, about 120 lines.

oeis-a364919.note: De Vlieger's 2023 conjecture (the sequence is a permutation of the positive integers) is stated faithfully as positivity, injectivity and surjectivity onto the positive integers. I re-implemented the Lean definition (A019565 via bits, rad, least unused m) and it reproduces all 66 data terms. Still labelled a conjecture. Elementary: every m is eligible at the infinitely many n with P(n) divisible by rad(m), and only finitely many smaller values can block it.

oeis-a289927.note: Barker's 2017 conjectured g.f. and order-8 recurrence for the p-INVERT (p(S) = 1-S-S^2) of floor(phi^k) (k >= 1) are stated faithfully, with a(n) = [x^(n+1)] 1/(1-S-S^2) in Q[[x]]; the controls match the data. Still labelled conjectures. Routine: floor(phi^k) is a Lucas number minus a parity term, so S is rational and the identity is algebra.

oeis-a345484.note: Wu's 2024 conjectured recurrence a(n) = 2a(n-1) - a(n-2) (n > 21) and g.f. are stated faithfully. A 'way' is a multiset of 7 positive squares, and Nat.nth with offset 1 is used. My own count reproduces the data, and all n >= 86 are terms. Still labelled conjectures. Routine: a finite check plus showing every large n has >= 7 representations.

oeis-a232868.note: Wu's 2018 conjectured recurrence (n > 10) and g.f. for the positions of the real integers in Kimberling's x+1 / i*x tree are stated faithfully. The construction is exactly the Mathematica loop (interleave x, x+1, ix, then DeleteDuplicates). I simulated it, confirmed the prefix property, and reproduced all 55 data terms. Still labelled conjectured. Routine: an explicit eventual pattern of the tree, proved by induction.

oeis-a297445.note: Kimberling's conjecture is that the recurrence sequence 1, 5, 11, 47, ... gives the least positive integer with base-3 up-variation n. The statement encodes up-variation correctly on LSB-first digits, and a brute-force search to 2*10^6 matches a(0..12). Still a conjecture in the entry. Elementary digit-minimality argument.

oeis-a346807.note: Wu's 2023 conjecture a(n) = n + 64 for n >= 8 (numbers that are sums of ten positive squares in >= 8 ways) is stated faithfully with multiset counting and Nat.nth offset 1. My count reproduces the data, and every n >= 72 is a term. Still labelled conjectured. Routine: a finite check plus an eventual-representation argument.

oeis-a232866.note: Kimberling's three conjectured formulas for the position of the integer n-1 in the x+1 / i*x tree are stated faithfully: a(n+4) = 2n^2+n+6, the g.f., and the cubic recurrence. The Lean list construction mirrors the Mathematica program, and my simulation reproduces all 50 data terms; Lst n already contains n-1. Still conjectured in the entry. Routine: an explicit pattern by induction.

oeis-a023408.note: Lowell's 2020 conjecture A023408(n) + A023402(n) = 9 for n > 1 is stated faithfully, using the unique k-digit {5,6} and {3,4} numbers divisible by 2^k. I checked that both definitions reproduce the OEIS data and the identity holds to n = 300. Trivial: x56(k) + x34(k) = 10^k (6+4 = 10, 56+44 = 100, 656+344 = 1000, ...), forced by uniqueness.

oeis-a345503.note: Wu's 2024 conjectured recurrence (n > 9) and g.f. for numbers that are sums of nine positive squares in >= 6 ways are stated faithfully. My count reproduces the data, and every n >= 65 is a term. Still labelled conjectures. Routine: a finite check plus an eventual-representation argument.

oeis-a226076.note: Barker's 2013 conjectures a(n) = 4a(n-3) (n > 9) and the g.f. for the greedy sum-free sequence of squares are stated faithfully. Greedy = least square not a distinct-subset sum of earlier terms, and the controls match a(1..10). Still labelled a conjecture. The proof identifies the terms as {4^k, 9*4^k, 289*4^k} past the start, and shows every other square is a distinct-subset sum by base-4 splitting plus a finite kernel check. A genuine argument, though elementary.

oeis-a074882.note: Israel's Aug 2026 conjecture (a(n) < n when n is not 1 or a prime power) is stated faithfully, with a(n) = #{k in [1, sigma(n)] : gcd(k,n) = 1}. I checked it for n < 20000. Still labelled a conjecture. Elementary: split [1, sigma(n)] into blocks of lengths d | n, each holding at most phi(d) coprime integers, and one block loses an extra integer.

oeis-a127710.note: Barry's 2007 conjectures are stated faithfully for every finite truncation, which determines the infinite lower-triangular inverse: the inverse of A(n,k) = 1/(n+1) for k <= n <= 2k is integral, and row n sums to the ruler function A001511(n+1). I checked both with exact rational inversion up to N = 40. Routine: the inverse is P^{-1} diag(k+1) with P the 0/1 pattern, which has an explicit integer inverse.

oeis-a332446.note: McEachen's 2023 conjecture (every prime p = 3 mod 8 is a term, i.e. A087808(p+1) = A087808(2p)) is stated faithfully, with A087808 defined by its recursion. Trivial: for any p = 8m+3, A087808(p+1) = 4(A087808(m)+1) = 2*A087808(p), so primality is irrelevant (42-line proof).

oeis-a284354.note: Barker's 2017 g.f., parity closed forms and recurrence for the 2D outer-totalistic Rule 899 x-axis readout are stated faithfully, with the background evolving under the rule (899 is odd). I simulated the CA and reproduced all 33 data terms. Still labelled conjectures. Routine: an explicit periodic pattern proved by induction.

oeis-a273847.note: Barker's 2016 conjectures for 2D Rule 969 are stated faithfully: a(n) = (2n+1)^2 for n > 4, the recurrence and the g.f. The count is over the central (2n+1)^2 square with the background evolving, as in the entry's program. My simulation reproduces all 47 data terms. Routine: an explicit pattern by induction.

oeis-a120123.note: Firoozbakht's conjecture that 139968 is the largest m = (digit product)*phi(digit sum) is stated faithfully as IsGreatest over positive m. It is still an unmarked conjecture in the entry. The proof is a length bound (m < 9^k phi(9k) against 10^(k-1)) followed by a kernel-certified pruned search over sorted digit tails: a finite check, so routine.

mo-430643.note: Spiga's inequality prod p_i^(a_i^2/4) <= r^(log2(r)/4 + 1 - l) for r = prod p_i^(a_i) with all a_i >= 2 and r not in {36,72,900} is encoded faithfully (Finset of primes, real powers, the same exceptions; empty s is harmless). The MO question (2022) has no answer. The proof takes logarithms, reduces to a quadratic inequality in S = sum a_i log2 p_i, and handles the supports {2,3} and {2,3,5} with rational log bounds. It is elementary but a genuine proof of an unanswered research-level question.

oeis-a269631.note: The conjecture that the greedy sequence (next = least unused number containing the decimal length of the previous term as a substring) is a permutation of N is encoded faithfully: 0 has digit list [0], and reversing digit order preserves infixes. The encoding matches the data 0,1,10,2,11,... The proof is a short elementary argument: injectivity is by construction, widths are unbounded, and at the first visit to each width L every number containing L is still available, so each number is eventually reached. Routine.

oeis-a284937.note: Kimberling's 2017 conjecture that 2n - a(n) is in {0,1,2}, where a(n) is the position of the n-th 1 in the fixed point of 0->01, 1->1100, is encoded faithfully. The proof file checks a(1..8) against the data. It is routine: both images have exactly half their letters equal to 1, so every prefix is nearly balanced.

oeis-a089640.note: Wu's 2023 conjectured recurrence and g.f. for the number of alternating {1,2}/{2,3} compositions. The recursive 'ways' definition reproduces a(1..22) of the data (proved in the file). The recurrence follows directly from the two-state transfer recursion. A 58-line routine identity.

oeis-a345487.note: Wu's 2024 conjectured recurrence and g.f. amount to: every n >= 94 is a sum of seven positive squares in at least 10 ways, and the first 10 terms are 70,...,94. The statement counts multisets of 7 positive integers with the right square sum and takes the nth term with Nat.nth, which is faithful. The proof (1588 lines) establishes the eventual inclusion via classical representation facts plus finite checks. Routine in substance, but laborious to formalize.

oeis-a020963.note: Wu's 2016 conjectured order-5 recurrence and g.f. for sum_{k>=1} floor(2(1+sqrt2)^(n-k)) are stated faithfully as a tsum over k >= 1 with integer powers (terms with k > n are 0). The file checks a(1..5). Routine: 2(1+sqrt2)^m equals a Pell-Lucas number minus the small conjugate, so the floors satisfy a linear recurrence with a periodic correction.

Erdos1042.erdos_1042.variants.universal.note: The FC 'universal' reading of EHP58 Problem 6 says every closed F of capacity 1 not inside a closed radius-1 disc admits, for infinitely many n, a monic f with roots in F whose set {|f|<1} has n components. It is research open: Ghosh-Ramachandran settle only the existential reading (examples exist) and conjecture the weaker limsup C_n/n = 1. The disproof builds a genuine compact counterexample, a pair of circles, with Harnack and harmonic-measure estimates (1979 lines). It does not use an unbounded or degenerate F. I found no earlier construction. The original existential question is solved on the site, but this variant is new.

FanelliMoscardelli.stability_threshold_t.note: The paper's Section 5 conjectures that ceil(|N|/2) is the true threshold for complete graphs (I checked the rendered PDF). The upstream Roommates definitions match the paper: one-based ranks, a single agent has rank delta_i+1 = N, and a pair blocks when both gain at least k positions. The disproof proves K(2m+1) <= m for m >= 3, so K(N) < ceil(N/2) for odd N >= 7. That contradicts the eventual equality. Two Palomar entries report the same disproof, but both are dated 27-28 Nov 2026, after the PR's commits (26 Nov, US time), and formal-conjectures issue #7848 shows no earlier claim.

arxiv-1801.06737.note: The statement is the conjunction of Conjecture 1 (g_n* non-increasing) and Conjecture 2 (the sufficient attractiveness inequality is necessary for g_1* = g_n* for all n) of Hsieh–Barmish–Gubner, in the paper's setting: i.i.d. bounded returns, support points Xmin < 0 < Xmax, E[X] > 0. gStar is a sup over K in [0,1), which equals the paper's max over [0,1] because g_n is monotone as K tends to 1, and the integrand is bounded there, so the Lean integrals are honest. Hsieh's 2020 follow-up (arXiv:2004.12099) proves only a multi-asset 'dominant asset' necessity result, not these conjectures. I found no other resolution.

arxiv-2606.27961.note: The statement is Conjecture 6.2 of Barcau–Paşol–Ţurcaş: for odd primes p, delta((Z/p^2)^2, pG) = (2p-1)^2. A set T bijecting onto (Z/p)^2 under coordinatewise reduction is exactly a transversal of the cosets of pG, and the minimum of |T-T| is stated with IsLeast. The paper (v1 only, 26 Jun 2026) proves only 3p^2-p-1 and a conditional result. I found no later resolution.

mo-396509.note: Pinelis conjectured that the best constant c in E|X-Y| - (1/2)E|X+Y-2Z| >= c E|X-Y| is 1/9 for iid log-concave densities, attained by exponentials. The statement gives IsGreatest of 1/9 plus equality for every Exp(r), with log-concavity in multiplicative form (zeros allowed). The best published bound is c = 1/10 (MO answer 488763, Mar 2025, which itself calls 1/9 conjectural). The question has no answer.

mo-488874.note: The question asks for loopless multigraphs with Delta(S)+Delta(G-S) > Delta(G) for every nonempty proper edge subset S, and for the minimal |E| for each Delta. The formalization splits multiplicities, which the question allows, and claims the sharp minimum: 0, 1, 3 for r = 0, 1, 2, (r-1)(3r+1)/2 for odd r >= 3 (10 for r = 3, matching the asker's computer search), and nonexistence for even r >= 4. The question has no answers. This is a substantive result (Petersen 2-factor and Lovász deficiency arguments).

Erdos344.erdos_344.variants.sqrt_two.note: The upstream variant (eventually |A ∩ [1,N]| >= sqrt(2N) implies subcomplete) is faithful to the erdosproblems text: countUpTo counts [1,N] and IsSubcomplete asks for an infinite AP with d > 0 inside the subset sums. The site still calls this 'still open' (page edited 28 Dec 2025, 0 comments, 0 proof claims), and the catalog's erdosState 'proved' refers to the Szemerédi–Vu constant-C main problem. The proof is a long new argument (Bergelson–Furstenberg–Weiss and Bohr sets). I found no earlier proof.

oeis-a160108.note: Barker's 2014 conjecture a(n) = 2a(n-6) - a(n-12) for the Lodumo_8 transform of the Fibonacci numbers. The sInf definition matches the transform and the data (a(0..14) are proved in the file). Routine: the closed form a(n) = (F(n) mod 8) + 8*#{j<n : F(j) = F(n) mod 8} plus the Pisano period 12.

oeis-a387957.note: Hutton's conjectured g.f. (1/4)(prod 1/(1-x^j)^4 - prod 1/(1-x^(2j))^2) for 4-coloured partitions whose colour sum is 1 (mod 4). The definition (multiplicity functions bounded by n; products truncated at n) is faithful and gives a(0) = 0, a(1) = 1. Routine roots-of-unity filter.

oeis-a223211.note: Barker's 2018 g.f. 6x(1+x)/(1-2x-4x^2) and Binet-type closed form for walks of length n-1 on the given 6-vertex graph (n X 1 arrays). The definition and the 9 edges match the entry, and a(1) = 6, a(2) = 18. Routine transfer-matrix computation.

oeis-a076935.note: Cloitre's 2002 conjecture that a(n) is floor(cn) or floor(cn)+1, for the real root c = 0.59749700868... of 1-2x+x^2-x^3+x^4-x^5, is encoded faithfully (the guards in the nested recursion always hold). The disproof is a certified table: a(61371) = 36670 = floor(61371c) + 2. I recomputed the sequence independently, and the first failures are at n = 61371, 61530, 72074. The entry still lists it as a conjecture. A finite computation, so routine.

oeis-a309952.note: Ianakiev's 2019 conjecture that k first occurs in the XOR-contraction sequence at A000695(k) (binary digits read in base 4) is encoded faithfully: pairs taken from the least significant end, an odd leading digit padded with 0, and a(0..15) plus a(19) checked. It follows immediately from Lang's recursion a(4n+r) = 2a(n) + [r in {1,2}], an 81-line routine proof.

oeis-a330910.note: Barker's 2020 g.f. and order-7 recurrence for subsets of {1..n+5} with gaps >= 5. The statement requires at least two elements, which the data a(0) = 0 and the n = 11 example force, so this is the correct reading; a(0..6) are checked. Routine linear-recurrence counting.

oeis-a273744.note: Barker's closed form, recurrence and g.f. for the partial sums of 2D Rule 901 (von Neumann outer-totalistic, single seed). The plane-with-evolving-background model and the central-square counting reproduce the data 1,9,34,83,... Routine: an explicit description of each stage by induction.

oeis-a269910.note: Barker's five conjectures (closed forms by parity, recurrence, g.f.) for 2D Rule 3 are stated as a conjunction. The background-flipping simulation in the plane, trimmed to |x|,|y| <= n, reproduces 1,5,1,45,1,117. Routine: the stages have a period-2 explicit shape.

oeis-a308034.note: Barker's 2019 g.f. and recurrence for 3-part partitions of n with some part not dividing n are stated faithfully. Routine: the all-divisor partitions correspond to 1 = 1/a+1/b+1/c, i.e. (3,3,3), (2,4,4), (2,3,6), so a(n) = p3(n) - [3|n] - [4|n] - [6|n], a quasi-polynomial.

oeis-a345482.note: Wu's 2024 conjectured recurrence and g.f. say that every n >= 70 is a sum of seven positive squares in at least 5 ways, with the first 13 terms 45,...,70 as listed. The multiset count and Nat.nth indexing are faithful, and the controls a(1..13) are proved. The same method as A345487 (classical representation facts plus finite checks) is routine in substance, though long (1359 lines).

oeis-a048200.note: The statement defines a(n) as the minimum length of a word in L (left rotate, List.rotate 1) and X (swap the two leftmost entries) that reverses 0..n-1, with no inverse rotation. My BFS reproduces the OEIS data 0,1,2,4,10,15,23,32,42 (allowing right rotation would give different values), so the definition is faithful. The Kuppili-Chitturi formula 3n^2/4-2n (even) and (3n^2-10n+15)/4 (odd) is stated for n>=4, because literally it fails for n<=3 (e.g. it gives 3 vs a(3)=2); that is a reasonable reading. Kuppili-Chitturi gave only the upper bound. CayleyPy (arXiv:2509.19162, Sep 2025) still lists the formula as a conjecture. Uskov et al.'s Nov 2026 proof of Glushkov's L/X diameter formula (Hexagon 2611.00039; Palomar 2 Nov 2026) concerns the diameter, not the reversal distance. The 951-line proof (matching rotation and swap lower bounds plus an explicit schedule) is substantive, and I found no earlier proof of the reversal distance. Statement PR #9768, proof PR #11755.

oeis-a192744.note: The statement faithfully encodes Mathar's two conjectured recurrences (2014, 2015) for the constant term of p(n,x) mod x^2 - x - 1, where p(0) = 1 and p(n) = x p(n-1) + n!; I checked the first terms against the entry's examples. Proving them is a routine holonomic/Fibonacci computation, done in the 123-line proof. Elementary; I found no recorded earlier proof.

oeis-a201686.note: The statement faithfully encodes Mathar's 2014 order-4 recurrence for a(n) = C(n, floor(n/2)) - 2 for n >= 4. The proof uses parity cases and factorial ratios. Routine and trivial; I found no recorded earlier proof.

oeis-a133552.note: Colin Barker's 2018 conjectured order-15 recurrence and rational g.f. for the number of binary words of length n with at most 4 ones in every 6-bit window. The Lean transfer-automaton (32 suffix states, five leading zeros, so 11111 is excluded at length 5) reproduces the OEIS data 1,2,4,...,37834 at offset 0 in my brute-force check, and both conjectured identities are stated coefficientwise. The proof is a routine finite transfer-matrix computation (16 tables plus linearity), so this is routine/trivial. I found no earlier proof. Statement PR #8704, proof PR #9947.

oeis-a006501.note: Mathar's 2011 conjecture is A006501(n) = A144677(n) + A144677(n-2). The statement defines both sequences by their o.g.f.s: (1+x^2)/((1-x)^2(1-x^3)^2), and 1/((1-x)^4(1+x+x^2)^2) as recorded in A144677 by Meijer in May 2011. With those, the claim is literally (1+x^2)B = B + x^2 B, and the 13-line proof is just that. The statement is faithful only to the extent that A144677 is identified with its recorded g.f.; its name refers to a 'quantum states' definition in a reference. It is trivial, answered by the formulas already in the two entries, and I found no explicit earlier resolution.

oeis-a096306.note: The statement is faithful: for every n > 0 the orbit of n under x -> x + (largest decimal digit) meets the orbit of 1 (A045844). This is Jason Earls's 2004 conjecture, still listed. No related entry (A045844, A095815, A101227) and no arXiv paper I found records a proof. The proof shows that every positive orbit passes through 10^k + 101 for all large k. I checked this numerically for k = 5 (n < 10^4) and k = 6 (5,000 starting values). It is a short (about 100 lines) but genuinely clever elementary argument for a 22-year-old conjecture.

oeis-a378616.note: The conjecture (greatest non-prime-power <= prime(n) equals prime(n) − 1 exactly when prime(n) is not a Fermat prime, i.e. off A159611) is stated faithfully; IsPrimePow excludes 1, which matches the data. Trivial: p−1 is a prime power iff p = 2^{2^m}+1. Unmarked in the entry, and I found no earlier proof.

arxiv-2603.18243.note: Hyman's Conjecture 3.17 states lim_{B→∞} #{b <= B : b is PERS}/(B-1) = 1/12, where PERS is Corollary 3.16's continued-fraction criterion on log10(b) at sample size N. Its evidence (ρ(1000..5000) ≈ 0.081-0.084) is at the survey depth N = 10,000, which the formalization fixes. The PERS predicate transcribes the criterion (some q_k <= N with a_{k+1} q_k > N log N). The disproof is elementary and robust. Every b in (10^(k+8), 10^(k+8)+10^k] has log10 b = integer + r with r tiny, so a_1 >= 10^6 > N log N, and the whole block is persistent. A convergent density L would then force L = 1 via 100000001*ρ(R_k) - 100000000*ρ(L_k) = 1. The same argument works for any fixed N, so the conjectured limit fails (it does not exist). This is a low-profile 2026 numerical conjecture, and I found no earlier refutation. Statement PR #7163, disproof PR #8540.

oeis-a254211.note: Alois P. Heinz's 2015 conjecture is that infinitely many n admit a length-n array over {1,2,3} with no equal neighbours and no prime leading or trailing partial sum. The Lean 'valid' predicate reproduces the OEIS data (1,0,0,0,1,0,...) in my brute-force check to n=16, and 'for all B there is a valid array longer than B' is the conjecture. The proof gives an explicit palindromic family H ++ k*[3,1,2] ++ ... whose prefix sums all have a factor 2, 3, 5 or 7. That is elementary but a genuine construction. Still a conjecture in the OEIS (last edited Nov 2025), and I found no earlier proof. Statement PR #6923, proof PR #7982.

oeis-a068598.note: The conjecture is Beregovsky's (2022; refit in Feb 2026 to c ~ 1.36): a(n) ~ a*exp(b n^c) with c ~ 1.54. It is formalized as: there exist a, b > 0 and c > 1 with ratio -> 1. The definition (maximal families of pairwise part-disjoint strict partitions of n) is faithful; I recomputed a(0..25) by brute force and it matches the OEIS data exactly. The disproof notes that a family is a set of disjoint subsets of [n], so a(n) <= (n+1)^n = exp(O(n log n)) = o(exp(b n^c)) for every c > 1. Any c > 1 fit is impossible, whichever value is chosen. The disproof is valid, elementary and robust, and I found no earlier note.

oeis-a384309.note: The statement faithfully encodes Sycamore's 2025 conjecture: every positive integer occurs exactly 9 times (1 occurs 10 times), and the last k-digit term is a(24*10^k - 7) = 10^k - 1, which is how the entry's index '23[k-1]93' decodes; the formal version even proves that all later terms are >= 10^k. The 402-line proof analyses the leading-digit counters in complete decimal blocks. The entry still says conjecture and I found no earlier proof. Non-trivial combinatorics.

oeis-a184894.note: Paul Hanna's conjecture is that the coefficient of x^(2m-1) in the m-th iterate of x+x^3 is ≡ 0 (mod 3) except at m = (3^j+1)/2. The statement proves the forward direction (a nonzero residue implies m = (3^j+1)/2). It also gives the exact residue C((3^j+1)/2, j) mod 3 at each candidate, and shows 3 | a(365), so the exception set is not exact. I verified numerically (Frobenius, up to m=1200) that the nonzero residues occur exactly at m = 1,2,5,14,41,122, and that m = 365 and 1094 are 0 mod 3, matching the binomial formula. So the statement faithfully resolves both readings of 'except at'. Not marked proved in the OEIS (last edit 2020), and I found no earlier proof. Statement PR #7532, proof PR #8115.

oeis-a132297.note: Barker's 2013 conjectures (closed form (15+(−1)^n−4n+6n^2)/8, order-4 recurrence, g.f.) are for the number of distinct digram-count profiles of binary words of length n. The formal 'Profile' matches the data (4, 7, 12, … from n=2) and Varshney–Goyal's definition of a second-order type (a multiset of digrams); that paper gives no closed count. Unmarked in the entry, and I found no earlier proof. Elementary combinatorics.

oeis-a112992.note: The statement faithfully encodes the comment that odd values of ceil(2^(2^k mod k)/3) are Jacobsthal numbers and even values are Jacobsthal + 1. It holds for any exponent m: 3J(m) + (-1)^m = 2^m gives ceil(2^m/3) = J(m) (odd) for odd m and J(m)+1 for even m. The value 2^k mod k plays no role. Trivial; I found no earlier written proof.

oeis-a156695.note: The statement is faithful to the entry's conjecture (which the statement credits to McEachen; the comment is unsigned): every odd n > 5 not of the form p + 2^a + 2^b (a, b > 0) is divisible by 255. The PR exhibits n = 275984581255575 = 3*5^2*241*257*59411893, which is = 15 mod 255. I re-checked independently (python, Miller-Rabin) that n - 2^a - 2^b is never prime for 1 <= a <= b <= 59. Known covering constructions (Crocker; Pan 2009; Ding-Sun-Zhao, arXiv:2607.05357) put Fermat numbers such as 17 into n, so they are consistent with the conjecture. I found no earlier non-multiple of 255. A genuine computational disproof.

oeis-a119659.note: The conjecture says (3,5,11), (5,11,17), (11,17,31) are the only consecutive prime-indexed-prime triples failing the triangle inequality. It is stated faithfully as pip k + pip(k+1) <= pip(k+2) ⟺ k in {1,2,3}, with pip k = prime(prime k). The proof uses explicit Chebyshev bounds ported from PrimeNumberTheoremAnd plus a finite check. Unmarked since 2006, and I found no earlier proof. Elementary but with real explicit-estimate work.

oeis-a328002.note: The statement faithfully encodes Luschny's 2020 conjecture: with q(n) = a(n+1)/a(n) in lowest terms, d(n) = num - 2*den has period 12 with pattern (1,2,3,3,3,2,1,1,3,6,3,1) from n = 0 (I checked the first values). The proof derives closed forms for even and odd n, gets q(n) - 2 = 3/(m+3) or 6/((m+1)(2m+9)), and checks the residues. Elementary; I found no recorded earlier proof.

oeis-a110166.note: Bala's conjectures for k >= 2 are stated faithfully: the number of k-ary words with #1 <= #0 is [x^n](kx + 1/(1+x))^n, with u(0)=1, u(1)=k−1, and the recurrence shifted to index n+2. They are unmarked in the entry, and I found no earlier proof. Elementary generating-function work (about 500 lines).

oeis-a110199.note: R. J. Mathar's Nov 2012 conjectured recurrence for a(n) = Σ_{k<=floor(n/2)} Catalan(k), with the definition taken verbatim from the entry, for n>=3. The statement is faithful. It is trivial: the differences vanish at odd n and equal consecutive Catalan numbers at even n, and (k+1)C_k = 2(2k-1)C_{k-1} finishes it. It is still a conjecture in the OEIS, not in Ekhad-Yang-Zeilberger's list, and I found no earlier proof. Statement PR #6962, proof PR #7776 (title not the id).

oeis-a364554.note: The statement is faithful to Ngom's 2023 formula conjecture: the primes p with T(k) = np are exactly the primes among (2r±1)/d and (r±1)/(2d) over factorizations n = dr, so the counts agree. The entry explicitly says '(Proof is welcome.)'. Correct and new, but elementary (p divides one of the factors x, 2x±1 of 2T(k)).

mo-506603.note: Lchencz (MO, Jan 2026) asked to determine all n×n matrices with det(B)det(B̄) = 0 for every square submatrix B and its complementary B̄. The statement gives a genuine classification over any field: the property holds iff some R×C submatrix has n + 2 rank A[R,C] < |R| + |C|. Empty R is included, giving det A = 0, so it is faithful. Sufficiency is Will Sawin's comment of 6 Jan 2026. Necessity, the new part, follows from Edmonds' 1965 matroid partition theorem applied to the columns of [I | A]. The proof uses that classical theorem, but the question had no answer, only partial sufficient conditions in comments, and I found no earlier statement of the full characterization. Statement PR #6349, proof PR #7351.

mo-312603.note: The formal statement matches the question exactly: U = nonempty finite unions of nondegenerate closed subintervals of [0,1], and conditions (a) f ≠ [0,1], (b) positive overlap with A and B, (c) each player's overlap is maximized by truthful reporting. The PR constructs such an f (a 'three sites' rule), so the answer is yes, contrary to the asker's guess. The only MO answer (2021) admits it is incomplete, since (c) fails when the chosen pieces overlap; the variant question 386375 is different and also unresolved. I found no earlier solution. Non-trivial construction.

oeis-a248121.note: The statement faithfully encodes Chai Wah Wu's 2022 conjectures for a(n) = floor(1/(1/n - pi^2/6 + H_n^(2))): the order-5 recurrence for n > 5, and the g.f. x(x+1)^2(x+2)/((1-x)^3(1+x+x^2)) with a(0) = 0. This needs explicit two-sided bounds on the tail of zeta(2) that are sharp enough to pin down the floor, which the 366-line proof provides. The entry still says conjecture and I found no earlier proof. Non-trivial but elementary analysis.

oeis-a145646.note: This disproves Barker's 2019 fitted g.f./closed form/recurrence for round(n^2·10^10/R). The statement fixes R = 10973731.568527 as in the entry's own Maple program, and that reproduces all 13 listed terms. The recurrence fails at n=15 (205035 vs predicted 205034). I checked that it also fails at n=15 for every CODATA Rydberg value (2018/2022). Trivial: a curve fit to 13 terms of a rounding sequence (Mathar already notes the entry is ill-defined), but the refutation is correct and robust.

oeis-a383307.note: The definition (n-digit numbers, with 0 as a one-digit number, whose digit range equals the unique mode) reproduces the data 1, 0, 30, 631, 8318, which I recomputed. The claim lim a(n+1)/a(n) = 10 is Spezia's 2025 conjecture, still listed. It is expected heuristically (the range is almost surely 9, and 9 is the unique mode with limiting probability 1/10), but proving the ratio limit takes real estimates (1,135 lines). Correct, new and modest.

oeis-a039799.note: The definition (max over S ⊆ [n] of |B_S ∩ B_{[n]-S}|, with B_S the sums x+y, x<y in S) and the claim a(n) = 2n-11 for n >= 14 (IsGreatest) faithfully render Rob Pratt's 2015 conjecture, which the entry still lists as a conjecture. Pratt himself noted that the upper bound would follow from 'at most three sums from each end', which was unproven. The value matches the data, e.g. a(14) = 17 and a(15) = 19. It is a correct and new but elementary combinatorial argument (278 lines).

oeis-a093345.note: Mathar's 2014 recurrence a(n) - 2n a(n-1) + (n^2-2)a(n-2) - (n-2)^2 a(n-3) = 0 (n >= 3) is stated faithfully, with the defining sum computed in Q; I checked that it reproduces the data. Still labelled a conjecture, and it is not in the Ekhad-Yang-Zeilberger list. Trivial finite algebra.

oeis-a240558.note: Mathar's 2016 recurrence -(n+2)(n^2-5)a(n) - 8(2n+1)a(n-1) + 16(n-1)(n^2+2n-4)a(n-2) = 0 (n >= 2) is stated faithfully for a(n) = 2^n n!/((floor(n/2)+1) floor(n/2)!^2), and I checked it numerically. The entry's Sage program gives a different, parity-dependent first-order rule, not this one. Trivial.

oeis-a157713.note: Mathar's 2016 recurrence n a(n) = 4(2n+1)(2n-3) a(n-1) (n >= 2) is stated faithfully for the closed form (2n+1)!(2n-2)!/((n-1)! n!^2 6), computed in Q; the definition reproduces the data. Trivial: a ratio of hypergeometric terms.

oeis-a193282.note: Mathar's 2014 order-4 recurrence for a(n) = (n!/floor(n/2)!)^2 is stated verbatim for n >= 4 in Q, and the definition reproduces the data. Still labelled a conjecture. Trivial (parity split).

oeis-a212495.note: Latimer's conjecture is that A212495(n) > A033036(n) for only finitely many n. It is stated as finiteness of {i : nth oddDigits i < nth evenDigits i}, with offset 1 matched to Nat.nth's 0-based index (0 counts as an even-digit number, as in the data). Elementary counting: 6^k even-digit numbers vs about 5^k odd-digit numbers below 11^k.

oeis-a131662.note: Barker's 2020 g.f. and order-9 recurrence for the numbers n such that every d in 1..12 divides n or n+1 are stated faithfully. Routine: periodicity mod 27720 = lcm(1..12) with 8 residues per period gives term(k+8) = term(k) + 27720.

oeis-a330816.note: Corneth's 2020 heuristic conjecture is that the sequence (reach 1 under k -> k/d(k) when d(k) | k, else stuck) is finite with exactly the 45 terms of his a-file. It is stated faithfully as 'n reaches 1 iff n is in the list', and the list agrees with the data. Still a conjecture in the entry. The 800-line proof is a genuine bounded inverse search: a predecessor of m is mt with t = d(mt) <= 4 d(m)^2, plus exponent bounds for primes >= 17.

OeisA179537.conjecture3.note: The upstream conjecture3 (n | sum_{k<n} (42k+37)(-1)^k a(k) for all n >= 1, a(k) = sum C(k,j)^2 C(k-j,j)^2 (-16)^j) is Z.-W. Sun's July 2010 conjecture as recorded in the entry. It is tagged research open at the pinned commit. In Epoch's OEIS Open data this exact conjecture (part2a_mod_n) was attempted by four models and failed (scores 'I'); only the mod p^2 companion part2b was 'accepted'. I found no proof in the divisibility-of-Sun-sums literature (Guo-Liu, Mao and others). The 480-line proof is a genuine argument (column decomposition, binomial recurrences, Abel summation, Catalan integrality).

oeis-a088862.note: Zumkeller's 2003 conjecture (for every n there is an integer with exactly n prime factors counted with multiplicity whose divisors > 1 form a binary prefix code) is stated faithfully: 'b/2^k = a' means a is a binary prefix of b, and IsLeast of a nonempty set is the same as the sequence being defined. Still labelled a conjecture. The proof takes p^n for a prime p outside a finite exceptional set, since a prefix collision forces (p-1)^d < 2^t <= p^d. Elementary but genuine.

oeis-a140831.note: Mike Jones's 2022 conjecture (infinitely many k with k and k+1 both terms) is stated faithfully. An 'inversion' means primes p < q dividing n with q^{v_q} < p^{v_p}, which is equivalent to the prime powers not increasing, since equality is impossible. Routine: an explicit progression k = 3324 + 44100t works.

oeis-a274504.note: The conjecture (primes with (p|14) != 1 are exactly those not = 1,3,5,9,13,15,19,23,25,27,39,45 mod 56) is stated faithfully, with the Kronecker symbol written as chi_8^e times Jacobi, which is standard for n > 0. Trivial: (.|14) is a character mod 56, so this is a finite residue check.

oeis-a163767.note: The conjecture tau_n(n) = n^k for n squarefree with k prime factors is stated faithfully, with a(n) counted as ordered n-tuples with product n. Trivial: it is a direct corollary of tau_m(prod p^e) = prod C(e+m-1, m-1), since each prime goes into one of n slots.

oeis-a290650.note: Frohlich's 2017 conjecture is that Bailey's sequence (a(1) = 1; halve if even, else multiply by n) is unbounded. The Lean recursion is a faithful shift, and the claim is 'for all B some term exceeds B'. Trivial (25-line proof): halving cannot continue forever, and each odd term is multiplied by an ever larger index.

oeis-a336838.note: Karttunen's conjecture is stated faithfully: for consecutive primes p < q and odd e, A048673(p) = (q+1)/2 divides the reduced numerator of the mean of the divisors of q^e = A003961(p)^e. The entry's own comment reduces it to the denominator not absorbing factors of (q+1)/2. Elementary: a lifting lemma for geometric sums, about 130 lines.

oeis-a224669.note: Barker's 2018 closed form, recurrence and g.f. for (n+1) x 2 matrices over {0,1,2} with every 2 x 2 block idempotent are stated faithfully. Idempotence is over Z, the convention that reproduces a(1) = 12. Routine: a transfer-matrix count.

oeis-a158960.note: Hasler's 2014 conjecture that the reduced denominator of H_n(1/5) is 5^n is stated with the physicists' Hermite recurrence at x = 1/5, which reproduces the data. Trivial: the entry already gives a(n) = 2a(n-1) - 50(n-1)a(n-2), so a(n) = 2^n mod 5 is never divisible by 5.

oeis-a071282.note: Barker's 2017 conjectured period-6 g.f. and recurrence a(n) = a(n-6) for the denominators of the order-3 Peirce sequence are stated faithfully as periodicity 2,3,1,3,2,3, with the Graham-Knuth-Patashnik insertion rule. Trivial: translating by 1 preserves the Peirce order.

oeis-a326691.note: Karttunen's 2021 'Conjectured' formula a(n) = gcd(n, 1+(n-1)n') (n' = arithmetic derivative) is stated faithfully for n >= 1; he had checked it only up to 2^27. Elementary: after multiplying by n, the reciprocal sum has integer numerator S-1 with S = sum n/p, and the proof compares gcd(n, S-1) with the derivative form prime by prime (repeated primes divide every cofactor). About 100 lines.

oeis-a102730.note: A102730(n) counts the m <= n whose binary m! occurs as a substring of binary n!. Greathouse (2011) conjectured it unbounded, against Zumkeller's 'bounded'. The statement (for every k some n has a(n) > k) is faithful, with the infix taken on LSB-first lists, equivalent by reversal, and it reproduces the data. Still open in both entries. The proof embeds the binary expansions of all factorials up to k! in a single n! by dyadic scaling: a genuine, if not deep, argument.

mse-2030706.note: Lehs's conjecture is stated faithfully: an infinite set of positive integers with no common divisor > 1, closed under sums of consecutive runs of its elements, must be cofinite. The gcd reading follows the asker's comments. The question (2016) has 0 answers and no counterexample in the comments. The disproof adds a super-exponentially sparse sequence of powers of two and shows with a kernel check that no block sum hits a hole. Elementary but not trivial.

oeis-a121451.note: Layman's conjecture for the maximum product over partitions into parts = 2 mod 3 is stated faithfully: 0 for n = 1, 3; 2^(n/2) for even n; 5*2^((n-5)/2) for odd n >= 5. The sup over Nat.Partition gives 0 if no admissible partition exists. Elementary: x <= G(x) for admissible parts and G is supermultiplicative, so induction bounds the product, and twos (plus one five) attain it. Still a conjecture in the entry.

oeis-a158623.note: Mathar's 2009 recurrence a(n) = 3a(n-3) - 3a(n-6) + a(n-9) is stated for the reduced denominators of prod_{k=2..n} (k^3-1)/(k^3+1), and the definition reproduces the data. Trivial: the product telescopes to 2(m^2+m+1)/(3m(m+1)), so on each residue class mod 3 the denominator is a quadratic polynomial and its step-3 third difference vanishes.

oeis-a084029.note: Murthy's 2003 conjecture is that only one term of the triangle (row n = first n n-digit multiples of n with digit sum n, padded with 0) is zero. It is stated equivalently: row 2 is {20} only, and every other row n >= 1 has at least n such numbers. Still a conjecture (entry last edited 2014). Elementary digit-block construction plus small cases.

oeis-a276674.note: The entry's conjecture (if x - lambda(x) = 2m > 0 then x <= 4m, lambda the Carmichael function) is stated faithfully and still listed. Trivial: lambda(x) is even for x >= 3, so an even gap forces x even, and then lambda(x) <= phi(x) <= x/2. Bookkeeping: #7381 merged first, but an earlier-created PR #7319 for the same file later replaced its content.

oeis-a340896.note: Lowell's 2021 conjecture is stated faithfully: n^2 lies in row n (multiples of n with fewer than 2d(n) divisors) iff n is a prime power, with 1 included as in A000961. Trivial: d(n^2) = prod(2e+1) < 2 prod(e+1) iff n has at most one prime factor.

mo-364377.note: MO 364377 asks whether an orthogonal non-signed-permutation A can, in every neighbourhood, move to B in O(n) with |b_ij| >= |a_ij| on the support of its nearest signed permutation P (strictly somewhere) and |b_ij| <= |a_ij| elsewhere. The statement transcribes this. The counterexample is the 7x7 weighing matrix (-I+S+S^2+S^4)/2, which is locally rigid with its zero pattern, so it works for every nearest P (the previous review checked the rank-21 condition). Both the MO and MSE posts have 0 answers (comments in 2025 still ask), and no earlier counterexample was found.

mo-47888.note: The formalization is faithful: f: Z^k -> R^k monotone ((x-y).(f(x)-f(y)) >= 0), g(p) = E f(X) with X ~ Multinomial(n,p) built by n categorical draws, and the claim that g is monotone on the simplex for all n, k >= 1. The disproof uses n = 1, k = 3 and f(x) = h(x_1-x_2)(0,1,-1) with h a monotone step, so g is linear and not monotone. The question (2010) has 0 answers. Correct and new, but elementary.

oeis-a037301.note: Konig's 2020 conjecture (A037301, equal base-2 and base-3 digit sums, never contains five consecutive integers) is stated faithfully, together with the run 10..13 from the entry. Still listed as a conjecture, and Spiegelhofer's paper on infinitude does not address runs. Trivial: five consecutive integers contain 4k+1 and 4k+2, which have equal binary digit sums but ternary digit sums of opposite parity (s_3(n) = n mod 2).

mo-184507.note: Cheritat's 2014 question asks whether L(y) = int_0^1 sqrt(1+f_x(x,y)^2) dx is C^1 for every C^1 f on [0,1]^2. The statement encodes this with derivatives within the closed square, and the disproof builds an explicit C^1 f (sine bands accumulating at y = 1/2) with L not differentiable there. The MO question has 0 answers, its comments only discuss the title's surface version, and the asker says the earlier MSE post got no answer. A genuine answer by moderately elementary real analysis.

arxiv-2008.08020.note: This is Vielhaber's Conjecture 23: the binary question-mark function ?_V has no derivative at rationals in (0,1). I checked the encoding against the paper. C_I(b) = 0^l 1 followed by the complemented low bits of b (the paper's example 14 -> 0001001), C_II is its bitwise complement, and iota_AD(v) = (v1)_2/2^{|v|+1}, so the \10* deletion and the appended 1 cancel numerically, as the statement notes. The formal claim (no extension of the rational values is differentiable at any p/q) is stronger than the conjecture for the continuous extension. The proof uses two one-pair tails giving distinct right secant limits. I found no prior proof. It is a modest analysis argument (about 200 lines).

OeisA179524.conjecture5.note: The upstream statement is Sun's 2010 congruence verbatim: sum_{k<p} (20k+17)a(k) ≡ p(10(-1/p)+7) mod p^2 for odd primes p. The proof reduces it by binomial reflection to a one-dimensional sum evaluated with Zudilin's WZ pair (Theorem 3 of arXiv:0805.2788), a known tool but a nontrivial reduction. The OEIS entry and formal-conjectures still list it as a conjecture. Searches of Sun's lists and follow-up papers found no earlier proof of this specific congruence. Confidence that no obscure earlier proof exists is moderate, not certain.

oeis-a001764.note: The statement is the conjunction of Callan's conjecture (permutations of [n+1] avoiding 4231 and 42513 that end with an ascent are counted by C(3n,n)/(2n+1)) and Burstein's conjecture (sum-indecomposable (2431,45231)-avoiders of size n+1). Callan's final-ascent refinement is not in Albert et al. (2003), who count only all and sum-indecomposable avoiders. The proof's 'strict jump queue' refinement is new work. Caveat: Burstein's part follows from PermPAL's verified 2022 specification for the symmetric class Av(1342,13254). I checked that 1 - 1/F reproduces the ternary numbers. So that half was implicitly settled, but nobody had stated it.

oeis-a384539.note: The statement says the zeroless numbers >= 10 for which one side divides the other at every decimal split are exactly the 132 listed terms. This matches the entry's conjecture and its b-file. The entry has only partial observations (Corneth) and a search bound of 10^25. The proof needs a genuine argument bounding the length (middle-split quotient analysis) before the finite check, so it is more than a pure computation.

oeis-a336278.note: The conjecture that sum_{k<=n} mu(k)k^4 changes sign infinitely often is stated faithfully: positive and negative values for arbitrarily large n. The proof is a Landau/Pringsheim oscillation argument for the Mellin transform of 1/zeta(s-r), using zeta's non-vanishing on the real segment and the existence of nontrivial zeros. This is a classical technique, but I found no published statement for these weighted Mertens sums, and the entry lists it as open. Substantive analytic number theory rather than a computation.

oeis-a336276.note: Same as A336278 with k^2. The statement (sign changes infinitely often) is faithful. The proof is the same general Landau-oscillation argument for all exponents r >= 1, applied to 1/zeta(s-2). I found no earlier proof for this specific sum. Classical method, substantive argument.

oeis-a024849.note: Wu's data-fitted recurrence and g.f. (May 2026) are stated over the entry's definition: the least m separating {|F(h+1)-tau F(h)|} = {tau^-h}. The proof derives the closed form a(n) = 2L(n-2) + [n odd] and checks the recurrence and g.f. A routine closed-form/g.f. verification.

oeis-a345486.note: Wu's recurrence/g.f. conjecture amounts to 'from some point on every integer is a term'. The statement counts partitions into seven positive squares, has controls a(1..13) matching the data, and the proof is a finite witness check plus a Lagrange-based tail argument. Routine.

oeis-a345483.note: This is the same kind of statement as A345486 (seven squares in six or more ways). The definitions are faithful and the controls a(1..9) match the data. The proof is explicit witnesses plus an eventual-surjectivity argument. Routine.

oeis-a345493.note: Eight squares in six or more ways: the terms are exactly the 9 sporadic values plus every n >= 70. The proof uses Lagrange's four-square theorem for n >= 427 and explicit checks below. The definitions and controls match the entry. Routine.

oeis-a202253.note: Kimberling's closed form 1+2*floor((2n^2+2n)/3) for Hardin's count of zero-sum triples in -n..n with bounded adjacent differences. The definition is faithful, controls a(1..6) match, and the proof is a direct residue-class count. Routine.

oeis-a297443.note: Kimberling's conjecture that the recurrence sequence gives the least positive integer with base-3 total variation n is stated faithfully. Total variation is the sum of |differences| of consecutive digits, matching A297440, and the controls match the data. The proof is an elementary digit-extremal argument with explicit lower-bound tables. Routine.

oeis-a321612.note: The statement (exactly {2,4,6,7,9,13,16,21,31} qualify) faithfully encodes 'all triangular t with k/2 <= t < k have k-t triangular', with the nonemptiness condition implicit in the data. I re-checked the definition numerically up to 20000. The finiteness proof is a short gap argument about adjacent triangular numbers near the midpoint. Routine.

oeis-a308159.note: Barker's g.f. and recurrence for the sum of largest sides of isosceles integer triangles with perimeter n. The definition reproduces the data (controls a(0..11)). The proof is a closed form plus a g.f. identity. Routine.

oeis-a232867.note: Kimberling's conjectured quadratic formula, g.f. and recurrence for the positions of -n in the x+1 / i*x tree. The Mathematica DeleteDuplicates construction is modelled faithfully and controls a(1..4) match. The proof analyses distance generations and counts. Routine.

oeis-a286807.note: The conjecture that the n-th iterate of 00->001, 1->101 (StringReplace semantics) has A132045(n) letters is stated faithfully, with controls for the listed iterates. The proof is a token recoding and induction. Routine.

oeis-a390208.note: The conjectured g.f. (1/3)(prod 1/(1-x^j)^3 - prod 1/(1-x^{3j})) for partitions with parts coloured {0,1,2} and colour sum ≡ 1 mod 3 is stated coefficientwise with truncated geometric series, which is faithful. It is an immediate roots-of-unity filter: F(omega) = prod 1/(1-x^{3j}) and omega+omega^2 = -1. Routine.

oeis-a086524.note: Murthy's conjecture (every prime ≡ 5 mod 6 is the mean of two successive terms of A086523) is disproved with p = 17. The greedy model of A086523 reproduces its data (5,17,29,53,41,...). All terms are ≡ 5 mod 12, so the only possible pair is (5,29), and 5 and 29 are not adjacent. The entry flagged no counterexample, though A086523 had a parallel refutation in 2008. A trivial disproof.

oeis-a377112.note: Kimberling's conjecture (every prime divides infinitely many a(n), with eventually periodic gaps) is stated faithfully via the 4x4 integer step on coefficients of 1, sqrt2, sqrt3, sqrt6, with a real-identity control. The proof shows the reduction mod p is eventually periodic, using the adjugate identity adj*step = -23*I. Routine.

oeis-a249968.note: Wu's conjecture that squares of terms end in 00 or 56 is stated faithfully. wrap(m) = 2*10^(d+2)+100m+25, with controls 16 and 14130. The proof is a short modular analysis (83 lines). Routine.

oeis-a269876.note: Barker's five conjectured formulas for the 2D outer-totalistic Rule 43 automaton. The rule bit s+2k, the plane evolution and the count on [-n,n]^2 follow the entry's program, and controls match. The proof describes the explicit stage patterns and counts. Routine.

oeis-a273443.note: Barker's closed form 4n(n+1) for n > 3, the recurrence and the g.f. for 2D Rule 721. The definition matches the entry's conventions, and controls 1,4,21,41,80,120,168,224 match. Explicit stage description. Routine.

oeis-a063656.note: Lowell's greedy characterization (a(n) is the least number > a(n-1) that is a square iff n is triangular) is stated faithfully. The terms are where floor(sqrt k) = round(sqrt k), with offset 0 and controls. Elementary. Routine.

oeis-a358696.note: Manyama's order-9 recurrence for boundary-covering cycles in the 5 x n grid. The cycle is an edge set that is connected, 2-regular and covers all boundary vertices, matching the definition. The proof is a certified transfer-matrix computation with a polynomial annihilator. Routine (finite linear algebra).

oeis-a203164.note: Mathar's recurrence a(n) = 48a(n-4) - 576a(n-8) and g.f. for e_{n-1} of the periodic sequence (4,1,2,3,...). I checked that the definition reproduces the data 1,5,14,50,224,... and the recurrence numerically. Routine.

oeis-a090413.note: Mathar's holonomic recurrence for the Chebyshev transform of 3^n, defined directly from the entry's g.f. via the Catalan series substitution. A standard D-finite verification of an algebraic g.f. Routine.

oeis-a329178.note: Barker's g.f. and recurrence for partial sums of Padovan(i+5)*Padovan(i+7) (A000931 indexing). The data offset is consistent. Routine linear-recurrence identity.

oeis-a046385.note: Pfoertner's conjecture (the sequence has no terms beyond the 17 recorded) is disproved by an explicit 79-digit palindrome: 2977792 * P, where P is a sparse palindromic prime certified by Pocklington. It has exactly 14 palindromic prime factors (2^12 * 727 * P), so a(14) exists and is not in the list. I verified the palindrome, primality and factorization in Python. Consistent with the entry's remark that other terms would need >= 18 digits. An explicit certificate.

oeis-a266982.note: Hurt's divisor-sum parity formula for the Rule 81 triangle. The automaton is run on the full line, rows are read -t..t, and indexing starts at t^2, which matches the entry. The proof describes the CA explicitly and uses the hyperbola parity of sum floor((n-2)/i). Routine.

oeis-a060765.note: Corneth's conjecture (if consecutive-divisor differences all divide n, then p-1 | n/p for every prime p | n) is stated faithfully with an explicit consecutiveness condition. The proof is a short elementary divisor argument (about 70 lines). Routine.

oeis-a004215.note: Neumann's count conjecture (#{m < 2^n in A004215} = A023105(n) - 2 for n >= 1) is stated faithfully. Membership is defined literally, and A023105 is the number of squares mod 2^n. Given Legendre's three-square theorem (the terms are 4^a(8b+7)), this is a direct count. The proof formalizes Legendre via Ankeny's argument, but the mathematical content beyond the classical theorem is routine.

oeis-a067576.note: Kimberling's conjecture says each column of T+1 is eventually geometric with ratio 2. The statement proves the stronger exact start row max(1,j) for column j+1, which agrees with his d(1..5) = 1,1,2,3,4. Rows are the numbers with i set bits, which is the same as 2^i || C(2m,m) by Kummer. Explicit formula 2^(i+1)-1-2^(i-j). Routine.

oeis-a341239.note: The conjecture 1 < r s n - floor(r floor(s n)) < 3 with r = 1+sqrt2 and s = sqrt2 is stated faithfully. It follows directly from floor bounds and the irrationality of sqrt2. Routine.

oeis-a269454.note: For distinct safe primes p, q not ≡ -1 mod 8, ord_{pq}(2) = phi(pq)/2. Such p are 5 or ≡ 3 mod 8, so 2 is a non-residue and ord_p(2) = p-1, and gcd(p-1, q-1) = 2 gives the lcm. Faithful and routine.

oeis-a394678.note: If (n!-1) mod n^2 is prime (n != 4), then n and n^2-n-1 are prime. The entry already notes, via Wilson, that a(p) = p^2-p-1 for prime p. The remaining composite case is trivial: n^2 | n! for composite n != 4, so a(n) = n^2-1 is composite. Faithful and routine.

oeis-a362069.note: Petrescu's conjecture (infinitely many consecutive pairs k, k+1 with k + digitsum(k^2) square) is stated faithfully. The proof is an explicit infinite family built by padding with powers of ten. Short construction. Routine.

oeis-a044279.note: Dale's digit-sum conjecture for numbers whose base-9 form contains 31 but whose predecessor's does not. The statement encodes this exactly, with Mathlib's LSB-first digits (so [1,3] means '31'). The proof uses decimal digit sum ≡ k mod 9 and the structure of the first numbers in each block. Routine.

oeis-a180195.note: Mathar's D-finite recurrence for the alternating sum of (j-1)!(j^2-j+1), stated within the offset. Routine telescoping.

oeis-a083137.note: The conjecture that the greedy coprime-palindrome sequence is infinite is stated as the existence of a full greedy sequence. The proof uses the palindromes 10^((M+1)!)+1, which are coprime to every b <= M, so a candidate always exists. Routine.

oeis-a134799.note: Finch's conjecture that the reduced denominator of the Newton iterate b(n) for 1/sqrt3 is 3^((3^n+1)/2) = 3*A134799(n). The proof is a 3-adic valuation induction. Routine.

oeis-a394454.note: Both claims (every prime divides C(2n,n) for infinitely many n, and the sum of distinct prime divisors is unbounded) follow at once from Kummer/Legendre and from primes in (n,2n]. Faithful and trivial.

oeis-a216971.note: Perry's 2012 conjecture says every entry T(n,k) (endofunctions of [n] with exactly k non-recurrent points mapped directly into cycles) is divisible by n. The statement is faithful: periodic points are the recurrent ones, and k ranges over 0..n-1. Divisibility is not apparent from Critzer's e.g.f., and the proof is a combinatorial argument (about 470 lines). I found no earlier proof. Moderate rather than deep.

oeis-a387471.note: The conjectured closed form for interior triple concurrences of equal-angle cevians in an equilateral triangle (m = 2n-1) is stated via trigonometric Ceva. d(m) counts ordered triples (i,j,k) with prod sin x/sin(pi/3-x) = 1, x = (i+1)pi/(3(m+1)), which matches the entry's R-function formulation, and each concurrency point has at most one cevian per vertex. The entry calls the formula conjectural (verified n <= 200). The proof classifies the solutions with a roots-of-unity bound on rational relations among six terms, in the spirit of Conway–Jones and Poonen–Rubinstein. Substantive. I found no earlier derivation of this count.

oeis-a374365.note: Granvik's 2024 conjecture: m is a term iff m has a prime factor = 1 mod 10. The statement uses the principal complex power (-1)^(2k/5) = zeta_5^k, exactly as the entry's Mathematica program does, with offset m>=1. Since primes = 1 mod 5 are odd, 'p = 1 mod 10' is the same as 'p = 1 mod 5'. The proof is short but genuine: an involution d <-> dp cancels the sum when such a p divides m, and otherwise linear independence of the powers of zeta_5 forces sum mu(d) d = prod(1-p) = 0 in Z/5, which is impossible. I found no earlier proof.

oeis-a057566.note: The floor formula (as corrected by Alper Ferudun, Oct 2026) is faithfully stated for n>=1 with Fin 3 x Fin n and the zero-cross-product test. Collinear triples are the 3*C(n,3) vertical ones plus one point per column in arithmetic progression, so a(n)=n^3/2-n^2+n+(1-(-1)^n)/4, which is already in the entry (Mathar 2010); the floor identity follows. Routine count.

oeis-a002791.note: Irvine's 2014 formula a(n)=4 sigma(n)-f(n mod 6). 4sigma(n)-a(n)=sum_{d|n,d<=4} d(4-d)=3+4[2|n]+3[3|n], which is f(n mod 6). One-line routine identity; statement faithful.

oeis-a274782.note: Bala's 2023 supercongruence a(np^r) = a(np^(r-1)) mod p^(2r), p >= 5. The statement defines a(n) by Bala's sum Sum C(n,k)C(n+k,k)C(k,n-k), which the entry derives from Eger's theorem; I checked it against all listed terms of the diagonal. The quantifiers match (n, r > 0, p >= 5 prime). The proof is substantial: a Legendre-type identity with a period-6 twist, plus Jacobsthal-Kazandzidis scaling. I found no earlier proof. General Dwork-crystal results (Mellit-Vlasenko, Beukers-Vlasenko) give only mod p^r here, and the October 2026 Bala-conjecture preprints (Blanco Gomez and others) do not list A274782.

oeis-a389591.note: Pol's conjectured identity a(n)=sigma(n)-A379379(n). The proof is a three-line case split: a divisor r is not counted in a(n) iff r=1 or r>2*prevdiv, iff r is odd with no divisor d satisfying d<r<2d. Routine.

oeis-a261681.note: Mathar's 2017 order-4 P-recurrence for 2^n+C(n,floor(n/2))-1, stated for n>=4 exactly as in the entry. The proof is a direct factorial computation split by parity. Routine holonomic identity.

oeis-a278415.note: Sun's 2016 conjecture that (a(pn)-a(n))/(pn)^2 is a p-adic integer for p > 3. The statement forms the quotient in Q and asks that p not divide its denominator, which is exactly p-integrality; the definition matches the data. The entry itself only claims the weaker (p^2 n) version. Pan-Sun (2026) proved the analogous conjectures for A277640 and A208425 but not this sequence, and I found no other proof. The proof file says it is an original argument.

oeis-a035378.note: Bala's 2023 mod-5 congruences for the expansion of Kontsevich's F(q) = Sum (q;q)_k about q = -1. Writing x = Y-1 and truncating at k <= 2n+1 is exact, because the k-th product is divisible by Y^floor(k/2); the first terms match the data. These congruences mirror the Andrews-Sellers / Garthwaite-Rhoades mod-5 congruences for Fishburn numbers (the expansion at q = 1). But Garvan, Ahlgren-Kim, Straub and Guerzhoy-Kent-Rolen all treat expansions at q = 1 (or F((1-q)^r)), not at q = -1. I found no earlier proof.

OeisA179524.conjecture3.note: The upstream statement (research open at the pinned commit) matches Sun's 2010 claim: Sum_{k<p} a(k) = 0 mod p^2 for p = 11,13,17,19 mod 20. Numerically this sum agrees mod p^2 with Sum C(2k,k)^2 C(4k,2k)/(-1024)^k. For that sum, Z.-H. Sun proved only the split case mod p (Legendre polynomials II, Thm 5.3), and his 2020 list still records the mod p^2 congruence as Z.-W. Sun's conjecture. I found no proof of either form before the PR. Some residual risk remains, because the Sun-conjecture literature is large.

oeis-a297402.note: Jackson's conjecture that the gcd over the first n odd primes equals the gcd over all odd primes.
