It is stated faithfully as initialGcd n | (p^n-1)/2 for every odd prime p (the reverse divisibility is automatic). Corneth's comments already show the gcd is a power of 2 and settle odd n. The even case is lifting-the-exponent with p = 3 among the first n primes. Routine.

oeis-a195334.note: Mathar's conjecture a(n) = 2*A023194(n). Odd k have even-divisor sum 0, and the even-divisor sum of 2m is 2*sigma(m), so the two sets correspond under k = 2m and Nat.nth matches. The statement is faithful (offset 1, Nat.nth at n-1). No prior public solution was found, but the argument is a two-line observation. Second review: Faithful and true. For odd k the even-divisor sum is 0, and for k=2m it is 2*sigma(m), so the two sets correspond by doubling, which preserves order. A one-line elementary argument, hence routine.

oeis-a247173.note: Mathar's conjectured D-finite recurrence. The power-series encoding (S^2 = P with S(0) = 1, and G*(2x^2+2x)*S = 1-3x^2-2x^3-S) determines G uniquely and matches the g.f. I checked the polynomial coefficients term by term against the entry. The proof derives an ODE from the algebraic g.f., the standard holonomic method. Second review: Faithful D-finite recurrence for an algebraic g.f.; true and checked. Standard holonomic-closure computation, hence routine.

arxiv-1804.09594.note: This is Kuca's Conjecture 3.1 (2018): for n = 2^k+1 >= 5, the even terms of V(2,n) are exactly 2, 2n and 2n^2+2. The Lean greedy definition (unordered, not necessarily distinct, exactly one representation) matches the paper, and I recomputed n = 5, 9, 17, 33 up to 40000 ([2,10,52], [2,18,164], [2,34,580], [2,66,2180]). No prior proof turned up on arXiv, Zenodo (the 2026 Funayama note covers only U-sequences), trureturing, thatnealpatel/proofs, openai/math or Palomar. The proof is a substantial 3277-line argument via Sierpinski-type dyadic rows, marked 'STATUS: NEW'. Second review: Faithful statement of Kuca's Conjecture 3.1; no prior resolution found. A 3277-line kernel-checked proof using Lucas/Sierpinski parity structure; a genuine new result, not routine.

oeis-a129147.note: Mathar's conjectured recurrence for c(x(1+2x)). The encoding 2x(1+2x)G = 1-S with S^2 = 1-4x-8x^2 matches the data, and the recurrence holds on the data. The method is the routine holonomic one. Second review: Faithful and true; a routine D-finite recurrence from an algebraic g.f.

oeis-a085267.note: Greathouse's conjecture a(n) = n+11 for n > 50 (every m >= 62 has at least 2 representations as a nonzero square plus a squarefree number, and exactly 50 terms are <= 61). The statement is faithful (k > 0, n-k^2 squarefree, so >= 1). I confirmed it numerically to 2*10^5. The proof is a large but elementary sieve plus a kernel check below 1.2*10^7; I found no prior proof. Second review: Faithful. The proof combines a kernel-checked sieve up to 1.2e7 with an explicit elementary sieve bound above that, which is a genuine effective version of Estermann. Jimenez Urroz's explicit paper proves the weaker one-representation, zero-square-allowed statement, so the claim does not appear to be already settled.

oeis-a391613.note: The conjecture is that every n > 5 equals x^2+y+z with x >= 1, y >= z >= 1 and lcm(x^2,y,z) a square. The statement is faithful and reproduces the data a(1..25); I checked n < 3000, and the entry reports n <= 150000. The 2651-line proof combines elementary square-scaling families with Legendre's three-square theorem (formalized via Ankeny), a Minkowski determinant-1 lemma, CRT and a genus pigeonhole step. No prior proof was found; the conjecture dates from Jan 2026. Second review: Faithful statement of a recent (Jan 2026) Sun conjecture with no recorded proof. Elementary (three-square theorem plus casework) but not a short argument from the entry, so not routine.

oeis-a060212.note: It disproves White's 2023 heuristic a(n) ~ n log n log(n log n) log log n. A Selberg upper-bound sieve gives #{q <= x} << x/log^3 x, which forces a(n) >> n log^3 n, incompatible with the conjectured order n log^2 n log log n; if the sequence is finite the equivalence fails trivially. The sieve code is reused, with credit, from site PR 2394 (Enamakel). This is a standard sieve argument against an obviously mis-scaled conjecture. Second review: A correct, unconditional disproof by a formalized Selberg upper-bound sieve. The sieve code is credited to PR 2394 from the same site, which is fine. The conjecture was heuristically implausible but never refuted in print; the disproof is standard analytic number theory, not routine.

oeis-a027116.note: Barker's order-5 recurrence for the triangle diagonal T(n,n+3) of A027113, for n > 7. The Lean triangle reproduces the OEIS data, and the recurrence holds numerically to n = 60. The proof expresses the diagonal through tribonacci numbers, a routine linear-recurrence verification. Second review: Faithful and true. The left part of each row is tribonacci (Pirc's comment), which makes a(n) a linear-recurrence sequence; a routine verification.

oeis-a372561.note: Karttunen's three conjectures, stated faithfully: A372555 = 7 on the 13th antidiagonal from 933 on, A372555 = 9 on the 30th from 58325 on, and A372555(A372560(n,k)) symmetric for n,k > 1. The grid construction reproduces A372560 (27,165,41,...; 233,933,... and 911,58325,...), and minCoins matches the least-Jacobsthal-count definition. An exact DP confirms the small entries (933 and 14933 give 7; 58325 and 933205 give 9; symmetric pairs agree). The 372-line proof uses base-4 digit-sum lower bounds and explicit representations. No prior proof was found. Second review: Faithful to Karttunen's three conjectures (it correctly targets the global-minimum count). The proof certifies minimum counts by base-4 digit-sum lower bounds attained by shifted representations, a genuine structural argument, not a finite check.

oeis-a221574.note: Barker's g.f. and order-4 recurrence (stated for n>=5, where all indices are terms) follow from the cubic a(n)=n^3-n^2+3n-1, which the proof derives by direct counting. The definition matches the entry's array condition, and no prior proof was found. Second review: Faithful (the n>=5 range for the recurrence is the correct reading) and true. It is an elementary count giving a cubic polynomial, hence routine.

OeisA179524.conjecture1.note: The statement matches Sun's 2010 conjecture exactly (p prime, p = 1 or 9 mod 20, p = x^2+5y^2, sum_{k<p} a(k) = 4x^2-2p mod p^2). Searches turned up proofs of the analogous Apery-number case (Wang-Sun) but none for this sequence, and Sun's 2025/26 survey still lists sibling x^2+5y^2 congruences as conjectures. The 6.9k-line proof uses modular forms and eta quotients. Second review: Faithful, with no prior proof of this exact statement found. The 6899-line proof reduces the sum to a twisted truncated 3F2 and redoes a Beukers-style CM/modular-forms argument on Gamma0(2) at (1+sqrt-5)/2. The method and the companion F_p(-1/1024) supercongruence are known (Beukers 2024), so the novelty is the reduction plus formalization. Still a genuine, non-routine result.

oeis-a247170.note: Mathar's order-5 recurrence is checked against the g.f. defined by its algebraic equation, with the square-root branch fixed by its constant term. I checked the coefficients term by term against the entry and numerically (also at n=5, which uses the [x^0]=0 coefficient). D-finiteness of an algebraic g.f. makes this routine. Second review: Faithful and true; a routine D-finite recurrence for an algebraic g.f.

oeis-a182088.note: With m = 30(n-1), the factors are 1+m, 1+2m, 1+3m and 1+6m, so Korselt's criterion gives Carmichael whenever all four are prime (Chernick-type). The 'not only if' part needs a witness such as n=2 (91 = 7*13 composite, C(2) Carmichael), which I checked numerically. Routine. Second review: Faithful and true. Part 1 is a direct Korselt computation (a Chernick-type universal form); part 2 is a single explicit witness already implied by the entry's data. Routine.

oeis-a001358.note: Rocchelli's second-order expansion of the n-th semiprime is a direct inversion of the known expansion pi_2(x) = x log log x/log x + M x/log x + o(x/log x) (Crisan-Erban, Integers 2021; Landau/Delange). The statement reads the conjecture with an o(1/log log n) error, which is the natural reading. The Lean work rebuilds Mertens and the PNT from earlier merged libraries, credited in the header. Second review: True, and faithful to the evident intent. It is a short inversion of the known two-term semiprime counting asymptotic (Crisan-Erban Thm 1), so mathematically routine despite the 5825-line formalization of the PNT-level inputs. Not a deep new result.

oeis-a155051.note: Mathar's recurrence for c(x^2)(1+x)/(1-x). The coefficients expand the entry's form correctly (I checked numerically, including the degenerate n=3 case). Routine. Second review: Faithful to one of the entry's two Mathar recurrences, and true; routine. If announced, say which of the two was proved.

oeis-a082957.note: c is the reciprocal density of {k : sigma(2k) < sigma(2k+1)}. Kobayashi-Trudgian (2020) give only 18.20018 < c < 18.547, which is not enough for c < 18.5 (that needs density > 0.054054). The 5.3k-line proof establishes both the density and the sharper bound, and I found no later improvement (the 2023-24 follow-ups treat other progressions). This looks like a genuine new effective density bound. Second review: Faithful. The open content is only the upper bound c<18.5, i.e. density >1/18.5, which sharpens Kobayashi-Trudgian's 18.547. The 5285-line proof does this with an effective kernel-checked density computation. The announcement should say that existence and c>18.2 were already known.

oeis-a192347.note: p(n,x) is expanded correctly from (1/2)((x+d)^n+(x-d)^n) with d^2=x+2, and the reduction mod x^2-x-1 reproduces the data (checked to n=19). Barker's order-4 recurrence follows from a linear recurrence on the reduced pair. Routine. Second review: Faithful and true. Modulo x^2-x-1 the map x -> phi or psi turns p(n,x) into a combination of four geometric sequences, giving the order-4 recurrence. Routine.

oeis-a193656.note: The Q-residue and downstep follow the A193649 definition literally, and the closed form 3*5^n - 2*4^n matches the data. Mathar's closed form and g.f. follow by computing the residue of a geometric row. Routine. Second review: Faithful and true; a routine closed-form evaluation.

oeis-a122122.note: Mathar's two 2017 recurrences fail with the current indexing (for example -24 at n=2) because a(0)=1 was inserted in June 2022. The statement shifts indices by one to the 2017 numbering, and I checked numerically that both recurrences then hold. This is a correct, documented repair. Routine closed-form verification. Second review: Faithful to the recurrences as Mathar wrote them (2017 numbering); the shift is justified by the 2022 EXTENSIONS line. True and routine (hypergeometric closed form). When announcing, mention the renumbering.

oeis-a355007.note: Mathar's 2023 conjecture T(n,k) = n*A056856(n,k) is stated for 1 <= k <= n. A056856 is defined through its listed row formula (coefficient of y^(k-1) in prod_{j=1}^{n-1}(j + n y)), which reproduces the data (row 3 is 2, 9, 9). Given that formula the claim is immediate: the coefficient is n^(k-1) times the elementary symmetric function e_{n-k}(1..n-1), which is n^(k-1)|s(n,k)|. Trivial. Second review: Faithful and true; immediate from the rising-factorial generating function of unsigned Stirling numbers, given A056856's row formula. Routine.

oeis-a308222.note: Kagey's conjectured formula a(n) = 2*A096033(n+2) is stated faithfully: isosceles sides a, a, b with 0 < b < 2a, gcd(a, b) = 1, Heron's 16K^2 = b^2(4a^2 - b^2), and A096033 from its definition as hypotenuse-minus-leg. I checked the identity for the first 63 terms. The proof uses Weimholt's characterization of A096033 (odd squares and 2t^2) and the classical halving of an isosceles Heronian triangle into two Pythagorean ones. Elementary and routine. Second review: Faithful and true. Halving the isosceles triangle gives a primitive Pythagorean triple, and the perimeters become 2*(odd squares >=9) union 2*(2n^2, n>=2), which is twice A096033 from its third term on. A short argument from facts already cited; routine.

RefactorableNumber.infinitely_many_conse.note: The formal-conjectures statement is Colton's 1999 Conjecture 2 (infinitely many n with n and n+1 refactorable, i.e. d(n) | n and d(n+1) | n+1), and it is faithful. Wikipedia and A036898 still list it as open, and searches of arXiv, Palomar and the web found no earlier proof. The 15 KB proof is a CRT-plus-sieve construction: it forces n = 3^a u and n+1 = 2^(e+2) v-type factorizations, then counts residue classes so that the remaining cofactors have controlled divisor counts. Prime-power divisor-count lemmas follow a sibling site proof (Zelinsky's progression conjecture). Substantive. Second review: Faithful statement of a 1999 conjecture listed as unsolved, with no prior proof found. The proof is a short (336-line) elementary sieve construction. That is surprising for a conjecture open since 1999, but it is kernel-checked against the upstream statement, so worth a human read before announcing.

oeis-a265942.note: Hanna's conjecture a(n) = 2 (mod 4) for n > 2, using the entry's own recursion with a(0) = 1. The definition reproduces the data, and I checked the congruence for n < 40. The proof is a short strong induction mod 4. Second review: Short elementary induction on the entry's recursion; true and faithful. Routine.

oeis-a226187.note: The conjecture is that a(n+1)/a(n) tends to exp(1/3), where a(n) is the least k with H_k > n/3. It follows from H_k = ln k + gamma + O(1/k), and the proof formalizes Hickerson-type bounds from A002387. The statement is faithful (firstAbove 0 = 1 only shifts one irrelevant term). This is standard asymptotics. Second review: True and faithful; it follows in a few lines from H_k = ln k + gamma + O(1/k). Routine.

oeis-a371898.note: Schulte's two conjectures: the column e.g.f. is k! t^k exp(t)/prod(1-it), and the signed row sums give the derangement numbers. The definition matches the name and the PARI rule. The proof converts the recurrence into E(k+1)(1-(k+1)t) = (k+1)t E(k) and telescopes the signed sum into d(n+1) = (n+1)d(n) - (-1)^n. These are standard generating-function manipulations. Second review: Both Schulte conjectures hold and are faithfully stated; they are e.g.f./recurrence identities provable from the defining recursion. Routine.

oeis-a172062.note: Mathar's conjectured order-2 recurrence (k = 5). I checked the expanded cubic coefficients against the OEIS formula and the encoding against the data, and the recurrence holds on all terms. This is the standard D-finite derivation. Second review: Algebraic g.f. coefficient recurrence; true and faithful. Routine.

oeis-a059992.note: De Vlieger's conjecture (Jan 2025) is that every highly composite number other than 2 and 6 is a record for the number of nonprime divisors (d(n) - omega(n), counting 1). The statement is faithful, and I checked it for all 42 HCNs up to 3*10^6. The 1133-line proof uses exponent-vector exchange arguments, a central-binomial estimate for large supports, and certificates for ten residual cases. No prior proof was found in trureturing, thatnealpatel/proofs, Palomar or the OEIS entry. Second review: Faithful statement of De Vlieger's inclusion conjecture, numerically sound to 1e24, and the proof is a genuine argument rather than a finite check. Proof header thanks another site user for an earlier plan, which is internal credit, not prior literature.

oeis-a192748.note: This is Mathar's rational g.f. for the listed terms. The name says 'constant term', but the data and the Mathematica program use the x-coefficient of the reduction; the statement follows the data and notes this explicitly (I checked a(1..3) = 0, 1, 4). The proof tracks the remainder pair through a linear recurrence and compares coefficients. This is a routine linear-recurrence verification. Second review: True and faithful to the data; the entry's name/data inconsistency is documented in the statement and does not change Mathar's conjecture. Routine.

oeis-a275027.note: Sun's 2016 conjecture: for p > 5, (a(pn)-a(n))/(pn)^3 is a p-adic integer, where a(n) = Sum C(n,k)^2 C(n-k,k). The entry notes that Sun proved only the p^3 n^2 version. The statement is faithful (p does not divide the denominator of the rational quotient), and I spot-checked p = 7, 11, 13, 17. The 1300-line q-analogue proof uses cyclotomic root multiplicities and a q-WZ identity of Tauraso, reusing Gaussian-binomial lemmas from the site's A179524 proof. No prior proof of the full (pn)^3 statement was found. Second review: Faithful and apparently new: the closest literature result (Wang-Sun 2012.05121) treats a sibling sequence. Proof reuses Gaussian-binomial lemmas from another site proof (OeisA179524), which is internal reuse, and cites Tauraso for a q-identity it uses as a tool.

oeis-a193661.note: Mathar's rational g.f. for the Q-residue sequence. The statement follows A193673's data and formula, binomial(n,k)(1+3^(n-k))/2 as the coefficient of x^k, rather than its inconsistent name, and says so; that reading reproduces the data. The proof shows 2*residue(p) = p(2)+p(0), giving 4a(n) = 7^n+3^n+2, which I checked on all listed terms. Routine. Second review: Faithful to the data and definition chain; true. Routine.

oeis-a364114.note: The statement faithfully encodes Bala's four claims: the p^{3r} towers and shifted towers for p>=5, plus the two mod p^5 congruences for p>=7 (with a(n) written as the binomial sum equal to [x^n] P_n((1+x)/(1-x))^3/(1-x)). I found no prior proof. The rbajaj5 supercongruence census (Oct 2026) still lists the A364118 combination 3a(p)-11a(p-1) as open, and the 2026 Blanco Gomez families do not cover Legendre cubes. Substantive p-adic proof (Kazandzidis, Wolstenholme). Second review: Faithful and true as far as checked. Small residual risk: the triple-convolution form is not obviously covered by Coster's Theorem 4 or Osburn-Sahu-Straub, but I found no published theorem implying even parts 1-2, and parts 3-4 (mod p^5) look new.

oeis-a027984.note: T is the Lucas array exactly as in the A027960 PARI program, and the computed a(0..14) match the data. Barker's recurrence (n>=4) and g.f. follow from Fibonacci/Lucas closed forms (cf. Greubel's 2025 formula). Routine. Second review: True and faithful; rational-g.f. identity. Routine.

oeis-a278613.note: The TRIP-Stern maps follow Mathar's Maple convention for (e,e,132), and the definition reproduces the 20 listed terms (I checked 16 numerically). The column sums obey a linear 3x3 system with characteristic polynomial t^3-t^2-2t-6, which gives Mathar's g.f. Routine. Second review: True; linear maps make it an immediate rational g.f. Fidelity rests on the Maple-convention reading of the TRIP maps, which is confirmed by all 20 data terms. Routine.

oeis-a158196.note: Mathar's order-3 recurrence for an algebraic (Catalan-based) g.f. The square-root branch is fixed by its constant term, and I checked the coefficients and data numerically. Routine D-finite algebra. Second review: True, faithful, routine algebraic-g.f. recurrence (one of the two recurrences in the entry).

oeis-a239204.note: Mathar's order-3 recurrence for an algebraic g.f. in sqrt(x^2-6x+1). I checked the data and the recurrence numerically. Routine. Second review: True, faithful, routine holonomic recurrence.

oeis-a135052.note: Mathar's order-5 recurrence for an algebraic g.f. in sqrt(1-4x+8x^3-4x^4). I checked the data and the recurrence numerically. Routine. Second review: True, faithful, routine algebraic-g.f. recurrence.

oeis-a273386.note: Barker's closed form, recurrence and g.f. for the partial sums of ON cells of 2D Rule 659, stated as in the entry (outer-totalistic bit 2k+c, background evolving, count in [-s,s]^2 as the program trims). My simulation reproduces all 129 b-file terms and satisfies all three formulas through n=125. Still marked conjecture; nothing found in formal-conjectures, Palomar, Epoch, trureturing/thatnealpatel lists or openai/math. Routine eventual-pattern induction. Second review: Barker/Wu conjectures for a Robert Price 2D CA entry (Rule 659). Definition matches the full b-file and all conjuncts hold numerically to n=170. No prior proof located. Routine: once the eventual CA pattern is established the claims are recurrence/g.f. identities.

oeis-a284351.note: Barker's g.f., parity closed forms and recurrence for the left x-axis of 2D Rule 899 read in base 10, as in the entry's program. Definition matches the full b-file and all conjuncts hold numerically to n=170. No prior proof located. oeis-a007097.note: Ordowski's 2015 conjecture prod_{i<=n} log a(i) ~ a(n) is stated faithfully, with a(0) = 1 and a(n+1) = prime(a(n)). The disproof shows R(n) = prod log a(i)/a(n) cannot tend to 1. Each step multiplies R by at least 1 + 1/(16 log a(n+1)), via a second-order lower bound on pi(x), and these factors diverge like log log log a(n). Numerically R(n) climbs slowly (0.33, 0.57, 0.75, 0.85 at n = 5, 9, 13, 17), so the failure is not visible in the data. The effective PNT is reused, with credit, from an earlier site PR and Arithmetica4 (machinery only). I found no earlier refutation. Second review: A correct disproof of a conjecture that looks true numerically, because the divergence is extremely slow. It uses an effective PNT adapted, with credit, from Arithmetica4 and PR 5370. Genuine and non-routine.

oeis-a286014.note: The conjecture (A286014 = row sums of A211343) is stated faithfully, with A211343 from its name (column k is 1, 2, 3, ... interleaved with k-1 zeros, starting at row k(k+1)/2). mo-191547.note: Newman's question (is {floor(n^(3/2))} a basis of order 3?) is stated as: every m is val(a)+val(b)+val(c) with val(n) = Nat.sqrt(n^3) = floor(n^(3/2)). The question has no answers; the comments cite only Konyagin's two-summand result for alpha < 3/2 and the exceptional-set bounds of Balanzario-Garaev-Zuazua, so I found no earlier proof. The 10 KB proof is an elegant explicit construction: near v^2 the increments of val are pinned between consecutive integers, opposite moves of two inputs sweep a full interval, and a third input lands the residual. Small ranges are certified by bitmasks. Substantive. Second review: Faithful to the main question and answered affirmatively by an elementary construction (slopes near odd squares plus a finite certified range). A residual caveat: an analytic 'every sufficiently large n' result for three summands at c=3/2 may exist in the Waring-with-fractional-exponents literature, which I could not fully survey. The full statement for every n appears new.

gillibert-geodesic-deletion.note: Gillibert's conjecture (posted 17 Nov 2026: in a finite connected vertex-transitive graph on >= 3 vertices, deleting the vertices of any geodesic leaves a connected graph) is stated faithfully. Geodesics are paths of length dist(u,v), and including the one-vertex case is harmless, as the docstring explains. The conjecture is days old. The only related Palomar entry refutes a different Gillibert conjecture (Equal Halves), and I found no earlier proof. The 164 KB proof is a genuine structural argument: Watkins atoms and connectivity bounds, short geodesics, and an antipode/kernel-disjointness argument for the general case. Substantive. Second review: Faithful (identical to the author's Lean statement), and a full proof (3030 lines, kernel-checked) of a very recent conjecture for which a concurrent Palomar entry claims only partial results. No prior settlement. Worth flagging the conflict with the Palomar 'remain open' description when announcing.

oeis-a028576.note: Chapoton's Feb 2026 conjecture (n | a(n) and n^2 | 3a(n)) is stated faithfully. The 640-line proof re-derives that congruence for the squared central binomials from scratch. Correct, and standard technique. Second review: True and faithful; very recent (Feb 2026) conjecture that is a fairly direct consequence of classical binomial supercongruences, so routine. Proof is a self-contained 650-line elementary argument.

mo-142880.note: The question's edited form asks whether argmax_Z(B_t - d|t|) <= a * argmax_R(B_t - d|t|) + b in stochastic domination, with constants allowed to depend on d (as a 2013 comment suggests). The statement encodes exactly this with signed argmaxes, a two-sided Brownian motion built from two independent Mathlib IsBrownianReal arms, and a.s. maximizers D and T; the hypotheses are satisfiable. The question has no answers; one comment sketches that the matching tail rates of the two argmaxes should suffice. The 150 KB proof carries out the reflection and tail estimates for both tails. Substantive. Second review: Faithful to the edited MO question; the only prior input is a heuristic comment, so a rigorous proof is new. Proof establishes matching tails exp(-d^2 x/2)/(1+x)^(3/2) and takes multiplier one.

mse-5079681.note: Ripa's Conjecture 1 (for n >= 10 the leading digit of the prime zeta value P(n) = sum_p p^-n equals that of 5^n) is stated faithfully. The MSE comments and GH from MO's accepted MO answer only show it for sufficiently large n, using the fact that log2/log5 is not Liouville; nobody had an effective all-n proof. The PR supplies one: a Beukers-Bennett Pade/integral approximation, with knots 0, 3, 128, separates 5^n from the next decimal boundary for n >= 5000, and a kernel-checked certificate covers 10 <= n < 5000. Substantive. Second review: Faithful, true, and the full n>=10 statement was not previously proved (only 'for n large' on MO). Credits to MSE/MO contributors are acknowledgements, not a prior complete proof.

Second review: Faithful; the site proof (Nov 28 2026) covers every n, which goes beyond the two partial results it cites (bipartite case; n>=160). It credits them openly; the proof method (induced-path/trace counting with a kernel-checked finite part) is its own, so the full result appears new, but the announcement should mention the n>=160 result from nine days earlier.

It holds for 6<=n<40. Routine certificate proof; no prior proof found. The statement credits @vivanpoddar, the PR ivillar. oeis-a023554.note: Dement's identity 2(n+5) = A022308(n+4) - a(n+1) is stated faithfully: the convolution definition reproduces the data, and A022308 follows its name-recurrence. oeis-a024472.note: Mathar's g.f. is stated after clearing denominators, with the signs normalised correctly. s = Lucas with s(1) = 1, t(i) = F(i+1), and k = floor((n+1)/2) match the name, and the definition reproduces the data. Routine.

oeis-a026975.note: Barker's order-8 recurrence for n > 7 is stated faithfully over the A026648 triangle as named (the extra T(n-2,k-1) term when n is even and k is odd). Second review: Faithful and true; Barker's linear recurrence. Routine.

oeis-a027117.note: Barker's order-6 recurrence for n > 9 is stated faithfully over the A027113 array exactly as named, with offset 4. The definition reproduces the A027113 rows and the A027117 data, and the recurrence holds for n < 150. Routine (tribonacci-type column closed forms). Second review: Faithful and true; Barker's recurrence, with the correct lower bound. Routine.

oeis-a038261.note: Meeussen's g.f. is stated faithfully, with a(n) = w(8n) for the 5-wave sequence A038201 as defined by its recurrence. The definition reproduces the data, and I checked the product identity to x^200. Routine: a multisection of the rational g.f. of A038201. No prior proof found (not in Fried's papers, the libraries or Palomar). Second review: Faithful and true; Meeussen's g.f. is the bisection of a rational g.f.; routine.

oeis-a041042.note: The comment 'Subset of |A002316|' is stated faithfully. The numerators of the sqrt(27) convergents come from the period [5;5,10] block recurrence (it reproduces the data), and A002316 (Lehmer's beta_n) comes from its 12 listed signed terms and the order-12 recurrence of its entry. Numerically every numerator up to index 30 appears among the |beta|. The proof matches the two recurrences in Z[sqrt 3]. Routine, and no prior proof was found. Second review: Faithful and true. Subset claim reduces to matching two linear recurrence sequences; routine.

oeis-a041243.note: Dale's signature conjecture a(n+32) = 5177198 a(n+16) - a(n) is stated over Mathlib's GenContFract.of (sqrt 133) denominators, offset 0, which reproduce the data. The CF has period 16 (11;1,1,7,5,1,1,1,2,1,1,1,5,7,1,1,22), and I checked the recurrence numerically for n < 150. It is an instance of the classical fact that convergents of a periodic CF with even period L satisfy q(n+2L) = t q(n+L) - q(n). Routine. Second review: Faithful and true; Dale's signature is the standard recurrence for convergent denominators of a period-16 CF. Routine.

oeis-a049638.note: Mathar's g.f. is stated faithfully. T(n,4) uses the entry's PARI formula (n+1)(k+1) - #{0<=i<=n, 0<=j<=k: gcd(i,j) > 1}, which agrees with the hidden-point definition of A049615 (u = i-x, v = j-y) and reproduces the data. I checked the product identity numerically. Routine: g(i) = 1 + 2[2|i] + [3|i] gives a periodic difference sequence. Second review: Faithful and true; eventually-periodic differences give the rational g.f. Routine.

oeis-a079670.note: Both of Stephan's claims are stated faithfully over all primes p in A080050: 8p divides gcd(2^p-1, F(p)) - 1, and a > 1 when p is not 1 mod 10. I checked both for every such p < 30000 (14 primes, including 11, 8501, 10867). No proof found in the entry, Fried's papers or the libraries. The proof is a genuine elementary argument: common prime factors are 1 mod p, 2 is a QR, odd prime factors of F(odd) are 1 mod 4, and the rank of apparition forces 8p+1 to be 1 mod 5. Not a template. Second review: Faithful and true, with a short elementary proof (orders mod q, rank of apparition, quadratic reciprocity). Not noted as proved anywhere I could find, though it is a listed conjecture in Stephan's 2004 collection.

oeis-a083807.note: The conjecture (infinitely many nontrivial perfect powers with digits in {0,4,6,8,9}, nontrivial meaning not 10^k times another term) is formalized faithfully. The proof uses the explicit family (2+20*10^k)^2 = 4 0..0 8 0..0 4, which ends in 4 and so is never 10^k times a term. A correct and easy resolution; no prior record of it was found. Second review: Faithful and true via the explicit family (2+20*10^k)^2. Easy problem, not a formalization artifact; routine.

oeis-a087734.note: Kurkov's recurrence a(n) = 2a(floor(n/2)) + (n mod 2) - A036987(n) for n > 1, with a(0) = a(1) = 0, is stated faithfully. f(0) = 0 replaces A035327(0) = 1, which is documented and needed to reproduce the data: a(1) = a(3) = 0. The definition matches the data, and the recurrence holds for n < 5000. Routine binary-length induction. Second review: Faithful and true; elementary binary-digit recurrence. Only one of Kurkov's four conjectures in the entry is claimed.

oeis-a129654.note: Statement faithful: the pairs (m,r) with m,r > 1 and P(m,r) = n, and Gutkovskiy's g.f. truncated to k <= n, which is exact because the k-th summand starts at x^(k+1). The proof is the bijection P(t+2,k+1) = t*T_k + k + 1. Brute force matches the g.f. for n < 60. No prior proof found. Second review: Faithful and true; a one-line bijection. Routine.

oeis-a129695.note: Mathar's order-4 holonomic recurrence for the Laguerre transform of the Jacobsthal numbers is stated faithfully for n >= 4, with a(n) taken from the entry's explicit sum. oeis-a133603.note: Statement uses the entry's own formula (a(n) = C(n) for odd n, C(n)+C(n-1) for even n), which reproduces the data. Routine Catalan identity.

oeis-a134635.note: Statement faithful: the A134634 triangle has Catalan borders and the Pascal rule inside; row sums match the data. Mathar's order-3 recurrence holds for n = 3..39. Second review: Faithful and true; routine P-recurrence.

oeis-a135582.note: The g.f. 1/((1-x^2 c(x))(1-x-2x^2)) is encoded faithfully: S^2 = 1-4x with S(0) = 1 and 2xc = 1-S fix c uniquely, so the hypotheses are not vacuous. oeis-a138164.note: Faithful: T is the series reversion of x(1-x^2) (T - T^3 = X, T(0) = 0, unique) and G = 1/(1-T-T^2) as in the entry. All seven quadratic coefficients of Mathar's order-6 recurrence are expanded correctly, and it holds for n = 6..59. oeis-a138904.note: Statement faithful to the first conjecture: among binary expansions of length n, the attained numbers of rotational symmetries are exactly the divisors of n. One direction holds because the symmetry count is n/period; for the other, the d-fold repetition of 1 0^(n/d-1) attains d. Checked for n <= 15. Elementary cyclic-group fact, routine. Second review: Faithful and true; short argument. Second conjecture of the entry is not claimed.

oeis-a139376.note: Same structure as A135582, with (1-x-x^2): the hypotheses determine G uniquely, and all seven coefficients of Mathar's recurrence are transcribed correctly. oeis-a145052.note: Faithful: for n >= 3 every cell lies in some 3x3 block, so the nonnegative entries are forced into {0,1} and Fin 2 loses nothing; a(n) = 0 for n < 3 matches the g.f. oeis-a156201.note: Faithful: the numerator of E_n(1/8) equals 8^n E_n(1/8) (checked for n < 25), and Gladkovskii's continued fraction is encoded by depth-N convergents with tail 1, claimed for n <= 2N. That truncation order is correct: depth 3, 6 and 10 agree through n = 7, 13 and 21. The proof derives exact tails via Laplace transforms of e^(-3t) sinh^k sech^(k+1)(4t), a classical Rogers/Stieltjes-type argument. No prior proof found. Second review: Faithful and true. It reduces by a binomial (Euler) transform to Stieltjes' classical continued fraction for the secant numbers, so routine; the proof is long only because of Lean series plumbing.

oeis-a156377.note: Same as A156201 with E_n(1/16), 64(k+1)^2 and 1+7x. The numerator equals 16^n E_n(1/16), and the depth-N convergents agree through n = 2N+1 numerically. The proof is the same classical Laplace-transform derivation of the continued fraction. No prior proof found. Second review: Faithful and true. OeisA79727.conjecture1.note: Bala's conjecture 1 (2024): for p in A003625 (p = 3,5,6 mod 7), a(p^2) = 8 + p^2 mod p^3. The formal statement matches the entry word for word, and I checked it numerically for p = 3, 5, 13, 17, 19. The proof extends the site's earlier conjecture-2 proof (PR 6898) with Lucas vanishing and C(2p^2,p^2)^3 = 8 mod p^3, using CM/Picard-Fuchs arguments. Epoch's runs on the sibling conjecture 2 all failed. I found nothing on Palomar, in Fried's four OEIS papers or in Z.-H. Sun's 2026 preprint arXiv:2611.16834. Second review: Faithful, open, and new as far as every tracker I could reach shows. The proof (230 KB) also proves conjecture 2 on the way. I did not audit the Lean itself.

arxiv-1912.11230.note: Best-Wanless Conjecture 31: t_ac + t_bc + t_ad + t_bd = 0 mod 4 for every Latin square. The statement matches the source, including its definition of transversals of the (n-1)x(n-1) Latin array (min(m,n) entries, no shared row, column or symbol) and all a, b, c, d, not necessarily distinct. Brute force over all Latin squares of order <= 4 and 300 of order 5 found no violation. The proof is a genuine algebraic argument using signed sums of products prod_s(z + c_s(U,T)). I found no prior proof on the web, Palomar or openai/math. Second review: A real 2019 conjecture, now proved by a parity/sign argument (66 KB Lean). I found no prior proof.

arxiv-2008.10398.note: Fink's Conjecture 1: for every k there are ample numbers (a(n) > n, where a is the recursive divisor count of Definition 1) not divisible by the first k primes. The Lean recursiveDivisors matches Definition 1 (a(10)=6, a(12)=16, a(216)=504 checked), and 'p <= k' is an equivalent way of excluding the first primes. The proof is an elementary mass argument using divergence of sum 1/p over primes > k. The source and later Fink versions list it as open, and I found no prior proof. Second review: Short and elegant, a Hille-style argument. It is new as far as I can find, though an expert might call it folklore-level.

arxiv-2101.07103.note: Counterexample to Estrada-Mugnolo Conjecture 4.13 (v2): two K4's joined through a path 0-4-5 on 9 vertices. I recomputed it in floating point: the hubs-attracting index is about 68.1, above the ordinary index 61. That violates R_0 >= R_{-1} under both the Moore-Penrose inverse (the formal choice) and the paper's V Lambda^+ V^{-1} spectral inverse, so the disproof does not depend on that modelling choice. The conjecture does hold on all connected graphs up to 6 vertices (consistent with the authors' search up to 8). The proof is a finite rational certificate, and I found no prior counterexample. Second review: The counterexample refutes Conjecture 4.13 under both readings of the hubs-biased resistance. The formal statement follows the paper's literal 'Moore-Penrose' wording, which is evidently not what the authors computed. The write-up should mention that, and should say that the same graph also breaks the spectral version.

arxiv-2510.24280.note: Counterexample to Conjecture 4 (FvF never worse than AvA for either player): S = {3,5,12,16,30}, heap 83 gives FvF (48,35) and AvA (47,36), which I recomputed independently. The Lean recurrence matches Definition 2 of the paper, with friendly maximizing and antagonistic minimizing the opponent's total over the tied moves. The authors only tested max S <= 25, which explains why they missed it (here max S = 30). The latest version (v2, Jan 2026) still states the conjecture, and I found no prior counterexample. Second review: A clean finite counterexample to a 2025 conjecture, verified by kernel evaluation and by my own recomputation.

mo-267889.note: The asker's proposed identity E|B\A| = E|B|(1 - E|A|/n) fails at n = m = 2. By hand: E|A| = 3/2, E|B| = 5/4 and E|B\A| = 1/4, while the right side is 5/16. The formal model (second sample of size |A| drawn conditionally uniformly) matches the question. The question has no answers or comments, so this is an elementary but unrecorded refutation. Second review: A correct refutation by the smallest case. It is trivial, but the question really was unanswered.

mo-298064.note: The inequality |S_0(t,m)| >= |S_a(t,m)| is refuted. The Lean witness is the degenerate m = t = 1 case over F_2 ([1] has trace 1 and no rank-1 1x1 matrix has trace 0). My enumeration shows the claim also fails in non-degenerate cases: F_2 with m = 2, t = 1 (1 vs 2), F_3 with m = 3, t = 1 (8 vs 9), and F_5 with m = 2, t = 2 (16 vs 21). So the refutation is genuine, not an edge-case exploit. The question has no answers. Second review: Correct disproof. For an announcement, a nondegenerate counterexample (e.g. q=3, m=4, t=3) should go next to the 1x1 one.

mo-313415.note: Affirmative answer: with f(n) = (n+1)^3 ceil((32/27)^{n/3+1}), m = 1/2 beats every other m in [0,1], for any coupling of the arrays. The statement asks for this for every joint distribution satisfying row-wise independence and the Bin(n,1/2) law, which is stronger than any reading of the question. The proof uses threshold 2^{n/3} with binomial and first-moment bounds, a real argument. The question has no answers, and I found no prior solution. Second review: A substantive affirmative answer (m=1/2 with exponentially many agents), formalized with explicit bounds. I did not audit the 50 KB Lean, but the mathematics is consistent.

mo-331165.note: Berger's conjecture (div(rho B x v) = 0 for all B forces v parallel to grad rho) is refuted with constant rho and constant v. That witness is degenerate, but the conjecture also fails for non-constant rho: the condition is v x grad rho = rho curl v, and v = grad(psi)/rho solves it for every psi. The formal statement (all nonzero B, positive differentiable rho, differentiable v) matches the question, and it has no answers. Second review: The refutation is correct, but the Lean counterexample uses constant rho, which the asker probably did not intend. The announcement should give the general solution v=grad(phi)/rho (e.g. rho=e^x, v=e^{-x} e_y) so it cannot be dismissed as an edge case.

mo-479805.note: Proof of Kiwi's binomial-cdf inequality (1): (F(k)+F(k+1))/((n-k)(F(k-1)+F(k))) is nonincreasing in n. The formal statement matches the question: 0 < p < 1, m < n, 1 <= k <= m-1, and the same grouping. I verified it in exact rational arithmetic for 2275 cases (n <= 15, five values of p) with no violations. The proof uses a beta-integral representation, integration by parts and moment positivity. The question has no answers, and I found nothing on Palomar. Second review: A genuine proof of an inequality that was unanswered on MO.

mo-513259.note: Both of joro's 2026 conjectures are proved: per(M^{-1}) = 1 mod 8 and 2 per(M) + per(M^{-1}) = 3 mod 24, for adjacency matrices invertible mod 8 or 24, with the inverse taken in ZMod, which is equivalent to reducing the rational inverse. I checked every graph on n <= 6 vertices (13917 and 12401 cases) with no failures. The proof (Ryser expansion over Boolean faces mod 8, a mixed-moment identity over F_3) is genuine. The question has no answers, and I found nothing on Palomar. Second review: A recent (July 2026) MO conjecture, proved in 63 KB of Lean. Nothing prior found.

oeis-a000247.note: L. Edson Jeffery's (2012) conjectured matrix identity: for n > 2, entry v_{n-2} of A^n * 1, with A the n x n tridiagonal unit-primitive matrix whose last diagonal entry is 1, equals 2^n - n - 2. The zero-based index n-3 is correct, and I checked numerically for n = 3..19. The proof is a short dynamic-programming induction on the top diagonals. The entry still labels the identity a conjecture, and I found no prior proof. Second review: Correct and faithful. A short dynamic-programming identity.

oeis-a002857.note: Mathar's 2022 conjecture A002857(n) = A055621(n) - A055152(n), proved by the bijection between Boolean functions with f(0)=0, f(1)=1 and families of nonempty subsets containing the full set, equivariant under S_n. The Lean definitions reproduce the OEIS data (1,3,20,996 for Post functions; 1,4,34,1952 for covers; 0,1,14,956 for proper covers; brute force n <= 4). Elementary, and I found no prior proof. Second review: True by a one-line bijection; routine.

oeis-a007062.note: Kurkov's conjecture A007062(n) = A057030(n-1) + 1 (n >= 2). The Lean P(n) block-reversal maps for both entries reproduce the OEIS data (first 24 terms of each, checked). The proof observes that on positions >= 2 the A007062 map is the A057030 map shifted by one, and inducts. Short and elementary; no prior proof found (both entries still say 'Conjecture'). Second review: Correct and routine. It also settles the site's open oeis-a057030, which should be linked or closed as a duplicate.

oeis-a013302.note: Both of Mathar's 2014 recurrences for A013302, with the sequence defined from Jovovic's e.g.f. (2-x^2)/(2 sqrt(1-x^2)). The proof also shows this equals cosh(log(1+x) - artanh x), so the definition matches the entry's name, and it reproduces the data. I checked both recurrences numerically for n <= 14. Routine holonomic-recurrence verification; no prior proof found. Second review: Routine g.f. recurrence.

oeis-a093210.note: Stephan's conjecture a(n) = A060477(n+4) - 2 is stated faithfully: T(n,k) = A051168(n+4,k+2), k=0..n, matches the Mathematica program of A092964 (k+1 for k=1..n+1) and the data rows 1; 2,2; 2,3,2. Checked first terms against A060477. The proof is a routine Moebius-sum interchange. No prior proof found (OEIS, trureturing, thatnealpatel, openai/math, Epoch OEIS Open, Fried's four OEIS papers). Second review: True and routine (total Lyndon count minus the two border terms).

oeis-a093726.note: He's 2026 conjecture Im c(n) = A317974(n+1)/A138573(n) is stated faithfully for all representations c(n) = (x+yi)/d, with the convergent recursion matching the entry's examples (c(3) = (8+4i)/5 gives 4/5 = A317974(4)/A138573(3)). The proof uses Bala's Gaussian Lucas sequence U(n) from A138573 (|U(n)|^2 = A138573(n)) plus a quadratic-form recurrence identity; routine. No prior proof of this specific identity found. Second review: Routine: a quadratic form in a Lucas-type sequence satisfies an order-4 recurrence.

oeis-a097180.note: Mathar's order-3 recurrence is stated faithfully for n >= 3; I checked symbolically that the expanded coefficients equal Mathar's factored ones and that the recurrence holds for the series of 2/((1-8x)+(1-8x)^(3/4)) up to n=40. Using the entry's g.f. as the definition (T^4 = 1-8x, T(0)=1) is standard. Proof is the routine algebraic-to-D-finite derivation; no prior proof found. Second review: Routine algebraic g.f. recurrence.

oeis-a100833.note: Israel's 2019 conjectured formula (1 if n=1 mod 3, 2 if n=2 mod 3, else 3+v2(n/3)) is stated for all n>=1 against a faithful greedy definition (least positive letter avoiding a palindromic suffix of length >=2 and a square suffix). I recomputed the greedy word by brute force to n=1500 and it matches. The proof is a genuine combinatorics-on-words argument (no palindromes, no squares via a ruler lemma, minimality). No prior proof found; note the statement credits @frido22 while the PR is by Salofe. Second review: Correct; a short combinatorics-on-words argument.

oeis-a106249.note: Barry's conjecture a(n) = Sum_{k<=n} Jacobi(2^k, 2k+1) is stated faithfully for all n>=0 with the entry's g.f. as definition. Since (2^k|2k+1) = chi_8(2k+1)^k is 4-periodic (-1 iff k=1 mod 4), the claim is elementary; checked to n=200. thatnealpatel/proofs has an A106249 file, but it refutes Lagneau's different left-half-plane conjecture, so it is not a prior proof of this one. Second review: Routine periodicity argument.

oeis-a107793.note: Disproof of Sloane's 2018 conjecture that A107793, relabeled (5->6, 4->5) and with the first two terms dropped, is a shift of A275925. The definitions (f-morphism limit S[3k+1], sigma-trajectory of 3) are faithful and reproduce both entries' data, and the statement allows shifts in both directions. Numerically the best shift (11) agrees only for 41 terms. In ~10^5-term windows no shift in [-20000,20000] even agrees eventually. The proof writes the relabeled word as a sigma-image and uses aperiodicity of A275925; no prior refutation found. Second review: Sloane's 2018 'appears to be a shifted version' is false: the two words share a language but are not shifts of each other. The disproof is genuinely new.

oeis-a110521.note: Mathar's order-5 recurrence for n>=5 is transcribed correctly, with the entry's g.f. 1/(1-(x+x^2)c(3x)) as the definition (6xc = 1-S, S^2 = 1-12x); it holds for n<40. Routine D-finite derivation; no prior proof found. Second review: Routine.

oeis-a112000.note: Mathar's first-order recurrence n(4n+5)a(n) + (2n+3)(n+2)(4n+9)a(n-1) = 0 is stated faithfully for n>=1, with a(n) = A111999(n+3,2)/2 and A111999 given by its formula-section recurrence (it reproduces rows -1; 3,2; -15,-20,-6). Checked for n<40. The proof finds closed forms for columns 0-2 by induction; routine. Second review: Routine closed form.

oeis-a119012.note: Mathar's recurrence for n>=3 (offset 1) is stated with correctly expanded coefficients, and a(n) = [x^n] of Deutsch's g.f. (the normalised form agrees with the g.f. as a series and reproduces 0,0,1,5,23,...). It holds for 3<=n<43. Routine certificate proof; no prior proof found. The statement credits @vivanpoddar, the PR ivillar. Second review: Routine.

oeis-a119936.note: Lang's conjectured a(n)/n^3 = A002944(n)^2 is formalized as lcm_j den(M^3(n,j)) = n*lcm(1..n)^2, with M^3(n,j) = (1/n) Sum_{i=j..n} (1/i) Sum_{k=j..i} 1/k, which matches the cube of the mean matrix. I checked it exactly for n <= 150; it reproduces the data 1,8,108,576,18000,... The proof needs an exact p-adic valuation argument (a lower bound from a column j = p^e). No prior proof found; Meijer's formula in A027451 is a related unproved statement. Second review: Correct and apparently new as a proof. The announcement should note Meijer's 2009 unproved formula in A027451.

oeis-a062091.note: Mathar's 2025 conjecture a(n) = 2*A062090(n-1) for n >= 3 is stated faithfully, with both greedy sequences built over running products (least positive even / odd non-divisor). The definitions reproduce both data lines, and the identity holds for n <= 40. It is essentially immediate from the two entries' (unproved, Munn-corrected) characterizations {2,4} U 2{p^(2^k)} and {1} U {p^(2^k)}, which the proof re-derives. Routine. Second review: Faithful and true; Mathar's identity is immediate from the Fermi-Dirac-type characterizations recorded in both entries. Routine.

oeis-a064873.note: He's 2025 conjecture a(n) = A064874(n - A064874(n)^2) is stated faithfully. a and A064874 are the nested Nat.find minima of the lexicographically least 4-square decomposition, offset 0, and the definition reproduces the data. I checked it for n <= 3000. The proof is a short minimality argument: n - b^2 = a^2+c^2+d^2 has first part 0, and a smaller second part would give a smaller first part for n. True but elementary. Second review: Faithful and true. He's conjecture is a definitional consequence of lexicographic minimality (proof is ~15 lines, no number theory). Routine; it is an easy problem rather than a formalization artifact.

oeis-a067016.note: Barker's closed form 2a(n) = -3 + (-1)^n + 4n for n >= 4 and his g.f. are stated faithfully. a(0..3) = 1,4,3,2, and a(n+1) = max over 0 <= i <= n of a(i)+a(n-i) for n >= 3, as in the name. The definition reproduces the data, and the closed form holds for n < 200. Routine strong induction on the max-plus recurrence; the entry already notes that the first differences are ultimately periodic. Second review: Faithful and true; Barker's closed form and g.f. Routine.

oeis-a073409.note: Ordowski's characterization (a(n) is the largest prime r <= 2n+1 with r*num(B_2n) == -den(B_2n) mod r^2) is stated faithfully over Mathlib's bernoulli. I checked it exactly for n <= 40. It is a short corollary of von Staudt-Clausen (in Mathlib): the primes satisfying the congruence are exactly those with (r-1) | 2n, and the den is their product. Routine. Second review: Faithful and true; Ordowski's characterization is a direct restatement of von Staudt-Clausen. Routine.

oeis-a187298.note: Tours = injective sequences of 3 squares joined by the listed moves, counted over all starts; Python DFS reproduces the OEIS data for n<=16 (so the k-step = k-squares reading and move set are right) and Hardin's quadratic for n>3. The statement combines the quadratic, Barker's g.f. (with a(0)=0) and the order-3 recurrence. No prior proof found in searched sources; routine translation-counting argument (shared lemmas follow this site's PR 23762 for another sequence, which is not a prior solve of this statement). Asymmetric moves (-1,0),(0,-1),(2,0),(0,2) match 'one space left/up, two right/down'. Second review: Definition reproduces the entry's data exactly and Hardin's quadratic plus both Barker conjectures check out. No earlier proof found anywhere; the empirical formula is still marked empirical on OEIS. Routine: a bounding-box finite check of the kind Corneth used for A186864.

So for any start with AY_k never 0, Y_k/|Y_k| has coordinate 0 tending to 0. I checked with an exact-rational simulation over 200k steps. The source puts no condition on Y_0, and the failure is not tied to the special start. Second review: Valid explicit counterexample at n=4 to a conjecture the asker had only computer evidence for. No answers on MO.
