Robert Israel's 2024 proof in parent A245869 gives recurrences in the length for fixed k (columns), not this row formula in k. Routine quasi-polynomial count. Second review: Israel's/MSE state-machine method would also give rows, but no row formula is proved there. Routine.

oeis-a130187.note: Lang's conjecture a(n) = A001147(n+1)/A000265(n+1) is stated faithfully from the e.g.f. -2(exp(x^2/4)-1)/x (z(2n+1) = -2(2n+1)!/(4^(n+1)(n+1)!), so r(n) = (2n+1)!/(4^n (n+1)!)). Checked to n=300. The proof is a direct reduction to lowest terms (the odd part of n+1 divides (2n+1)!!). No prior proof found; routine. Second review: Elementary valuation argument; no earlier written proof found.

oeis-a370726.note: The 'only 1's and primes' conjecture is stated faithfully (nest(n-2, n+3), n>=3); I checked n<1500. The proof shows a(n) = (4n-3)/gcd(4n-3, A) and that 4n-3 divides q*n*(n-2)! for q = 1 or a prime, via a prime-power bound. The sister entry A356360 (2n-1 version) was solved earlier on this site with a simpler argument; this case needs the extra large-prime-factor analysis. No prior proof found. Second review: Proof: a(n) divides 4n-3 and the factorial part removes every factor except one large prime. No earlier proof found, including Bouras's own 2025 paper.

oeis-a240722.note: Mathar's order-2 recurrence (n>=2) for the log-derivative of the A186997 g.f. is stated faithfully: the radicals are pinned by squares and constant terms, and the coefficients match -(3n-1)(2n+1)(n+1), 2(21n^3+14n^2-2n-1), 8n(3n+2)(2n-1). I checked it to n=60 with the entry's binomial-sum formula. Routine algebraic/D-finite certificate; no prior proof found (iis crawl, Lean lists, BG, Fried). Second review: Holonomic recurrence of an algebraic function, proved by an annihilating-operator certificate.

oeis-a059145.note: The hierarchical construction W3{2,2}* is encoded with the ruler function: element k is [[r,r+1,r],[r+1,r+2,r+1],[r,r+1,r]], r = A001511(k); this reproduces the A059131 and A059144 data, and a(n) = partial sum of the first 2^(n+1)-1 terms of A059144 matches A059145. Barker's closed form 3(2^(n+4)-11-3n), recurrence and g.f. then follow from Legendre's formula. Routine; no prior proof found. Second review: Routine: the sum of the ruler function over 1..2^m-1 is 2^(m+1)-m-2. The reconstructed definition is the only real fidelity risk, and it matches 13 data terms.

oeis-a159769.note: Mathar's order-4 recurrence (n>=5) is stated for the explicit root of the entry's quadratic g.f. equation (x-2)x f^2 + (2x^2-2x+1) f + (x-1)x = 0; my series expansion matches the data (with a(0)=0) and the recurrence to n=30. Routine D-finite certificate. Not in the iis recurrence batches or other sources checked. Second review: Holonomic recurrence from an algebraic g.f., proved by an operator certificate.

oeis-a300388.note: Bala's congruence b(p) == b(1) = 5 mod p^3 for primes p>=5, p != 11, with b(n) = [x^n] A(x)^n and a(n) from Bizley's recurrence, is stated faithfully (b(p) is asserted to be an integer). I checked b(p) mod p^3 for p < 60 (p = 11 fails, as excluded). The proof uses Jacobsthal-Kazandzidis binomial congruences, with base lemmas reused from this site's earlier A375180 proof; the A300388 result itself is new. The sister A300386 (k=7) was solved on the site later the same day. No prior proof found. Second review: A Jacobsthal-Kazandzidis argument; the base lemmas come from this site's own A375180 proof. No earlier proof of this case found.

oeis-a082935.note: The conjecture (for n != 19 the first digit sum of a(n) is already n; for 19 it is 199 then 19) is stated faithfully: smallest palindrome whose decimal expansion begins with n and whose iterated digit sum reaches n at some stage k>=1. Only 19 is exceptional because any palindrome starting 19 ends 91 with sum >= 20. The proof header says it is ported from the author's 'DemosMathNT' Lean project, which I could not find publicly (GitHub repository search: none; code search HTTP 429, gap). No prior proof in the entry (Wilson checked n<=100). Elementary digit construction. Second review: The proof is a port of the solver's own (apparently private) DemosMathNT formalization; I found no public earlier source. If DemosMathNT turns out to be public and dated earlier, this becomes known.

oeis-a190038.note: Barker's g.f. and recurrence (n>8) for column 6 of Hardin's A190041 are stated faithfully (nondecreasing, last entry 6, each entry after the second equal to one or the sum of two distinct ones of the preceding three); my DP with that definition reproduces the data to n=21. The proof is a finite transfer computation. The parent table lists only empirical formulas, and no iis or other prior proof was found. Second review: Routine transfer computation.

oeis-a190039.note: Same model as A190038 with entries 0..7 and last entry 7; my DP reproduces the data (eventually 20n-60). Barker's g.f. over (1-x)^2 and recurrence (n>7) are faithful, and the proof is a finite transfer computation. No prior proof found in the parent table, iis or other sources. Second review: Routine transfer computation.

mse-2306090.note: The two empirical functional identities (2) and (3) are stated for K(a,x) = ((a-1)x-1)/(x+1) 2F1(1,ax;2+x;1/a), on the convergent ranges a>2 (which needs |1/(1-a)|<1) and a>1. I checked them numerically. The question has no answer; comments only note that (1) is Gauss's continued fraction. The identities follow from the classical Pfaff and z -> 1-z transformations with contiguous relations (the proof uses Euler integrals), so the result is true and new as an answer but classical in method. Second review: Classical hypergeometric transformations (Pfaff/Euler integral); open on MSE, no answer found.

oeis-a208601.note: Barker's g.f. and order-7 recurrence for 7-bead rotation necklaces with labels -n..n summing to 0 are stated faithfully (Quot by cyclic shifts, Fin 7 addition); a(1) = (393+6)/7 = 57 checks. Via Burnside (Howroyd's formula in A208597) a(n) = (N_7(n)+6)/7 with N_7 a degree-6 polynomial for n>=3, so the conjecture is routine (precedent A208995). No prior proof of the row found. Second review: Routine consequence of Burnside plus the A201552 formula; nobody had written the row-7 consequence as proved.

Arxiv.1701.08900.second_moment_one_extra.note: A disproof of Pittel's conjecture (stated in arXiv:1701.08900 / MOR 2019 after Theorem 1.3: E[S^2] = O(E[S]^2) when n2/n1 -> 1) for d=1. The FC model (n firms, n+1 workers, complete uniform strict rankings, Gusfield-Irving stability, all firms matched) matches Pittel's. The proof shows E[S] <= 10n/log n and E[S^2] >= e^-75 n^2/(115200 log n) at n = 16P^4, so the ratio grows like log n. Web search found no earlier refutation. Substantive research-level result. Second review: Substantive new disproof: the second moment exceeds the squared mean by a factor of about log n. No prior settlement found.

tarski-finite-basis-semigroups.note: Major claim: no partial recursive procedure decides finite basedness of finite semigroup tables (Volkov 2001 Problem 2.1; still listed open in 2026 surveys, e.g. arXiv:2602.18805, Araujo et al. arXiv:2610.02500). The statement reads faithfully: semigroup tables, identities as magma terms with Holds over all assignments, Entails as equational consequence over all magmas (associativity is itself an identity of T), Partrec on tables. The 20k-line proof is the PR author's (Abel Czupor) own Turing-machine-to-finite-monoid reduction, which he published on his website on 26 Nov 2026 asking for review; no earlier proof by anyone else found. Lean settles correctness given the statement; independent human review of the reduction is still pending. Second review: At origin/main 9c65461c4, I compiled proofs/tarski-finite-basis-semigroups.lean (19,797 lines, merged in #29945 and fixed in 6b9bc6d59) together with the catalogue statement, using Lean v4.33.1 and the site's Mathlib build. It compiled with no errors. `#print axioms OMA.solution` gives only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. A root-namespace guard (example : type_of% @_root_.OMA.S_tarski_finite_basis_semigroups.main := _root_.OMA.solution) also passed. The file contains no sorry, axiom, opaque, implemented_by, native_decide, extern or set_option. It assumes no external theorem: halting undecidability is proved inside the file by a diagonal argument (P455EffectiveMachine.no_self_decider), and Computable functions are linked to its machine model through Mathlib's TM2/Partrec compiler. McKenzie's theorem and tiling results are not used. The statement is faithful. FinitelyBased means a finite list R of binary-term identities whose semantic consequences over all magmas in Type are exactly the identities of the table (Birkhoff/completeness; associativity can go in R). Decidability means no Partrec p : List (List ℕ) →. Bool that halts correctly on every IsSemigroupTable (square, entries in range, associative, nonempty). This is the standard promise formulation over a genuine encoding, and it is not restricted to monoids or an extra signature. The images of the reduction happen to be monoids, which only strengthens the result. The problem was open in Volkov's survey and is still listed open in 2026 sources (arXiv 2602.18805, 2610.02500). I found no competing resolution. The manuscript's strategy is mathematically sensible: products of Jackson-style factor monoids of word sets that encode tile rectangles; halting gives isolated identities w0≈w1 that need unboundedly many variables; non-halting gives bounded-rank derivations plus the finite n-variable fragment. Human refereeing of the manuscript is still pending, but the Lean certificate is complete on its own.

RudinsConjecture.rudins_conjecture_uniqu.reason: The formal 'uniqueness' says that for all N>=6 every non-trivial progression attaining Qmax(N) has difference exactly 24. At N=6 the progression 120n+49 (49, 169, 289, 529) attains Q(6)=4, which refutes that claim trivially. The literature 'super-strong' conjecture of González-Jiménez–Xarles asserts uniqueness only up to equivalence and only for N = GP_k + 1 >= 8, so the formalization (all N>=6, literal q=24) is stronger than the real conjecture. The disproof exploits this mismatch and says nothing about the actual conjecture.

Bugeaud06.problem_10_6_variant_1.reason: The proof is a genuine, elementary construction: m enumerates {a*2^t : 1 <= a <= floor(log t)+1}. Density for every irrational xi follows from Dirichlet's theorem plus doubling, and consecutive ratios are >= 1 + (1/2)/log n. But Bugeaud's Problem 10.6 ('find a very rapidly increasing sequence...') is open-ended and not a precise statement. 'IsGenuinelySublacunary' (ratio floor 1 + c/log n, i.e. growth only about exp(cn/log n)) is a threshold the formalizers chose themselves, and the same argument works with any unbounded multiplier bound A(t). So it is not what Bugeaud asks, and proving it does not solve Problem 10.6. At most it settles a weak, catalogue-invented variant.

Green44.green_44.reason: The disproof only works because the formalization quantifies over all N, with no 'N sufficiently large' condition. It takes N = 100000 and the 1000 primes in [20011, 30161], which are < N^{9/10} = 31622 only because N^{1/10} < 10. Each A_i is the block of residues 10002..10001 + floor(p_i/2), so all of [1, 10001] survives and 10*|remaining| = 100010 > N. For large N (any N > 10^10) every prime is below N/10, and this trivial block trick is impossible. Green's question (from Erdős, contrasting with the large-sieve range p < N^{1/2}) is about the asymptotic regime, so nothing was learned about the real problem.

Erdos354.erdos_354.parts.ii.reason: The formal statement reads 'what if 2 is replaced by some gamma in (1,2)' as an EXISTENTIAL over gamma. The proof (a port of Kenta Kitamura's development) just picks gamma = sqrt(golden ratio) and shows that a SINGLE floor sequence floor(gamma^n alpha) is complete for every alpha>0. The second sequence and the hypothesis that alpha/beta is irrational are never used, which shows the formalization has removed the actual content of the question (whether, or for which, gamma in (1,2) the two-sequence statement holds as it does for gamma=2). This does not answer the question as erdosproblems.com poses it.

mo-93022.reason: The formal statement takes literally the question's 'that is' clause: v is connecting if for all p != q some k > 0 gives p.v^k = q or q.v^k = p. It then asks for such a v of length <= n-1 whenever one exists. The disproof is a 5-state, 3-letter automaton with a reset letter, checked by decide. It has a connecting word of length 6, and every word of length <= 4 is constant or preserves a nontrivial 2-colouring. Under that literal reading the counterexample is valid. However, the question is not precise or self-consistent. It asks about words whose 'underlying graph is connected' (Berlinkov's one-cluster setting), and in the comments the author says one may also assume that w takes A into one state. A constant map is never connecting in the literal sense once n >= 3, so the literal clause cannot be what was meant. A commenter also notes that assumptions are missing, which makes the answer obviously 'no'. Under the graph-connectivity reading the counterexample fails: its length-1 reset letter has a connected (one-cluster) functional graph. So the disproof settles a literal reading the author's own clarifications contradict, not a precise open question.

Erdos40.erdos_40.reason: The upstream erdos_40 is a 'question value' statement: {g | g -> infinity and Erdos40For g} = erdos_40.answer, where answer is a sorry placeholder. The PR proves only that this holds if answer is replaced by its own OMA.answer. OMA.answer is {g | g -> infinity and for all k there is T >= k such that every p in maximalProfiles k T violates a finite inequality against sqrt(i)/g(i)}. The proof gets there by rewriting with erdos40For_iff_finite (a compactness truncation to finite sets with representation count <= k) and finite_iff_profile_obstruction. So the 'answer' is a mechanical restatement of the defining predicate Erdos40For through finite truncations, not an explicit characterisation of the admissible g. The file header admits that the criterion 'does not settle whether there is any divergent denominator satisfying it', so it does not even settle the weaker variant or Erdős #28. The extra side results (log-band and fourth-root counterexamples) are partial and are not the stated problem. erdosproblems.com still lists #40 as open with 0 proof claims; this is a trivialised answer, not a solution.

mo-407245.reason: The MO question asks for the smallest l (as a function of k,n, or even an asymptotic bound) such that any l equipartitions of a kn-set force a pair to share a block in at least half of them. The formal statement does not give an answer: it defines threshold k n through hasOrthogonal k n 3 and hasOrthogonal k n 4, which are brute-force `decide` searches over every family of partitions, and only proves that the minimum is 3, 4 or nonexistent depending on those uncomputed predicates. The proof is the easy reduction: a pair that meets at most once can't reach r/2 for r=3,4, and repeating 4 pairwise orthogonal equipartitions cyclically defeats every r >= 3. Peter Taylor's comment under the question already gives this repetition idea (using Kirkman's 7 orthogonal partitions). The real content, namely for which (k,n) 3 or 4 mutually orthogonal equipartitions exist (for k=n this is the existence of 1 or 2 MOLS of order n, so e.g. k=n=6 gives 4), is left undetermined. The theorem therefore restates the question in terms of an unsolved design-existence predicate rather than settling it.

mo-148821.reason: The MathOverflow question (no answers, no comments) is open-ended: 'what can we say about |M_1 ∪ ... ∪ M_b| compared to a maximum b-matching, is anything known about the ratio?'. It gives no precise conjecture or candidate value, and the statement file says so itself. The formal 'answer' does not compute the ratio. It proves that p/q is guaranteed iff a finite integer certificate exists (`certified b p q`: labels, weights and linear inequalities over subsets of Fin b). That is an LP-duality/blow-up characterisation, which in effect restates the question as a finite linear program. It gives no explicit bound, does not even recover the 1/2 the asker noted for b = 1, 2, and says nothing about how the ratio behaves as b grows. The Lean proof (Farkas lemma plus a blow-up construction realising the dual) is a real argument, and legalRounds does faithfully encode successive maximal matchings. But it does not settle the source question, which is not a precise yes/no problem.

oeis-a346214.reason: The disproof attacks only the second conjunct, the finite formula T(n,n-j) = A002884(n)/(A002884(j)·2^(n-(j-1)^2)), stated 'for j < 2n'. It refutes that at n = 2, j = 1, where T(2,1) = 1 but the formula gives 6/4. The range 'j < 2n' is plainly a typo by Critzer: it allows every j < n, and the formula already fails at n = 3, j = 2 (1 vs 14) and at n = 4, j = 2 (315 vs 420). It holds in the checked cases with 2j < n (n = 3, j = 1: 21; n = 4, j = 1: 1260; n = 5, j = 2: 104160), so the intended statement is evidently 'for n > 2j'. The formalisation copied the typo literally, and the counterexample exploits only that. The actual conjecture is the limiting distribution lim P(X_n = j) = ∏(1-2^-i)·2^((j-1)^2)/A002884(j), together with the corrected finite formula, and the PR does not touch it. So the conjecture has not really been refuted.

oeis-a124352.reason: Barker's g.f./recurrence conjecture (and Mathar's equivalent form) is still marked as a conjecture in A124352 and A307933. The proof is a genuine 117-state transfer-matrix argument. However, the formal statement never mentions the antiprism or Hamiltonian paths. `a n` is defined as the output of an agent-written frontier/connectivity dynamic program (masks, addEdge, forget, closing), and the only link to the OEIS quantity is a docstring claim. The real mathematical step, that this program counts directed Hamiltonian paths of C_{2n}^2, is assumed rather than proved. Given the program, the recurrence is just Cayley-Hamilton bookkeeping. I ported the program to Python and it matches brute-force counts for n = 3..6 (240, 816, 2400, 6480) and the data up to n = 13, so it is very likely correct. But the Lean theorem does not certify the conjecture as stated: it proves a property of a custom algorithm, which is a degenerate encoding unless that algorithm is formally tied to the graph count.

Erdos691.erdos_691.note: Erdos asks for 'a necessary and sufficient condition' on A for M_A to have density 1, which is an open-ended request. The formal statement erdos_691.answer = (fun A => (multiples A).HasDensity 1) is satisfied by the tautological answer. So it accepts any equivalent predicate and cannot tell a real answer from a restatement. The submitted OMA.answer says that A meets every 'AdmissibleTest'. A test is an arbitrary infinite sequence of finite divisor-closed sets on prime blocks satisfying a harmonic-mass retention inequality, so the criterion quantifies over an uncountable family of obstruction certificates. It is a dual reformulation of the Behrend property, not an arithmetic condition on A. The forum thread notes that the analogous finite-approximation criterion is the classical Davenport-Erdos fact (Hall-Tenenbaum (1.3)) and does not count as a solution. The file says it is a port of github.com/Ghuffy1/erdos691, and erdosproblems.com/691 remains open. The proof is valid but does not solve the problem as posed.

Erdos357.erdos_357.parts.ii.bigO_version.note: The question is 'how does f(n) grow / find a good explicit g with f = O(g)'. The real open problem is whether f(n) = o(n). The formal statement f =O[atTop] answer is trivially satisfied by answer(n) = n, since a strictly increasing sequence in [1,n] has at most n terms. So it is vacuous. The submitted answer (44273/90000)n + 2 sqrt n + 177792 is again linear, so the Big-O conclusion carries no information beyond the trivial bound; the sharper constant (about 0.4919 < 1/2, said to be from Chandler Snively's 2026 preprint) is invisible to the statement. Known upper bounds on the page and forum are (2/3 - 1/512)n (Coppersmith-Phillips), about 0.8727n (Beker), and a claimed n/2 + O(n^{2/3}) (Lenthall-Cleary, July 2026). The PR itself concedes that 'whether f(n)=o(n) remains open'. Not a solution.

Erdos692.erdos_692.parts.ii.note: Erdos asks where, for fixed n, delta_1(n,m) attains its maximum. The formal statement only requires some function answer(n) at which the maximum over m > n+1 is attained. The submitted OMA.answer(n) is literally the argmax of the exact density, computed as residue counts mod m!, over the candidates m in [n+2, n+2+A+B], where A = (3^{2(n+1)^2})! and B is a factorial of a factorial. This is a brute-force argmax of the very quantity asked about, with a tower-type cutoff. It proves that the maximum exists and is attained below an astronomically large bound, but it gives no information about where the maximum lies, which is what Erdos asked; the PR concedes 'the cutoff is too large for practical computation'. erdosproblems.com/692 (Cambie: superpolynomially many local maxima) gives no closed form, and the question remains open.

Erdos732.erdos_732.parts.i.note: Erdos asks whether there are reasonable necessary and sufficient conditions for a sequence (X_i) to be block-compatible, i.e. realizable as the block sizes of a pairwise balanced design. The formal 'question value' statement accepts any predicate equivalent to membership in blockSizeProfiles n. The submitted OMA.answer says that s is sorted and that a coefficient of prod over all T subset of [n] with |T|>=2 of (1 + x^{term T}) is positive. By the proof's own lemma coeff_pos, that coefficient is positive iff there is a family of blocks covering every pair exactly once with the size multiset s. So it is the definition of block-compatibility re-encoded as a generating function, i.e. exhaustive search. The PR says 'this criterion makes no efficiency claim'. This is a restatement, not a solution.

Erdos1017.erdos_1017.upper_bound.note: Erdős asks to 'estimate' (sharpen) the clique-partition number f(n,k) for k > n^2/4. The formal 'upper_bound' only asks for some function with f(n,k) <= answer(n,k). Any known bound satisfies it: the API lemma f <= k, or Erdős–Goodman–Pósa's n^2/4. The supplied OMA.answer is min(n^2/4, k - C(r,2) + 1) with r = n - (C(n,2)-k). That is EGP plus the elementary bound 'a clique on n-q vertices, then the remaining edges one by one'. No matching lower bound and no asymptotic estimate is given. The one-sided statement is essentially vacuous as a formalization of the problem, so problem 1017 is not solved.

Erdos422.erdos_422.variants.growth_rate.note: 'How does f grow?' for Hofstadter's Q-sequence is formalized only as a one-sided bound f =O(answer), with answer supplied by the solver. OMA.answer = n, and the proof is f(n) <= n, which is built into the IsHofstadterQ predicate itself (it requires f(n-1) < n so that the recurrence is defined). The file also proves f(n) > c n infinitely often for c < 1/2, but the solution does not use it, and neither describes the actual growth (conjecturally f(n) ≈ n/2 with chaotic fluctuations). It is not even known that f is defined for all n. The answer is the trivial bound, so nothing about problem 422 is settled.

Erdos450.erdos_450.note: Erdős asks how large y(eps,n) must be, i.e. for an estimate of the threshold's size; the page discusses regimes such as y ~ 2n for eps << 1/n and no finite y at all for larger eps. The formal statement asks for exact equality windowThreshold eps n = answer eps n with an unconstrained answer function. The proof's OMA.answer is just a finite sup over residues x, r modulo P = lcm(n+1,...,2n-1) of a 'cutoff' solving the periodic counting inequality, i.e. the definition of the threshold re-expressed as a brute-force computation over one period. This proves only that the threshold is computable from periodicity and says nothing about how y(eps,n) grows in eps and n. The formalisation admits this tautological answer, so the open problem is not solved.

arxiv-2205.09212.reason: The source ('Primal Conjecture', §11 of Marrero–Acuña) is the vague implication 'phi_a op phi_b == phi_c (mod 9) => exists Z_a, Z_b with Z_a op Z_b = Z_c'. The paper then asks whether all members of the class are solutions or only some, and writes '... => ¬∀ Z_a, Z_b / Z_a op Z_b = Z_c'. The formal statement fixes the strongest reading: every z in column c is exactly x op y for some x, y in columns a, b. The disproof (5+6 -> 2, z=2) exploits a small-number edge case of exactly that reading. The paper itself signals the ∀ version need not hold, and the natural ∃ reading is trivially true. The source is not a well-posed problem, and the 'disproof' does not refute anything the authors claim.

oeis-a026796.reason: Beck's comment reads a(n+4) = b(n), with a = partitions with least part 3 and b = partitions with twice as many 1s as parts. The statement takes the n+4 literally, and the disproof only uses n=0: a(4)=0 but b(0)=1, from the empty partition. Numerically a(n+4)=b(n) fails at n=0,2,5,7,8,…, whereas a(n+3)=b(n) holds for every n<30 that I checked. So the comment has an evident off-by-one (the entry has offset 0 with a(0)=0 prepended in 2014), and the intended identity a(n+3)=b(n) is untouched. The disproof exploits the indexing slip, not a mathematical counterexample.

oeis-a100682.reason: A100682(n) = floor(C(n+3,4)^{1/4}) has offset 0, and Greathouse's comment reads a(n) = floor((n−3/2)/24^{1/4}) except n in {0,1,6,17,2403,5318}. Taken literally in A100682's indexing, as the statement does, the formula fails at almost every n (all n < 6000). The listed exceptions are exactly the n < 6000 where floor(C(n,4)^{1/4}) ≠ floor((n−3/2)/24^{1/4}), so the conjecture is about A000332 indexing, i.e. a(n) = floor((n+3/2)/24^{1/4}) with exceptions n+3 in the list. The disproof (n=2: a(2)=1 vs 0) exploits the shift by 3; the intended conjecture is untouched.

oeis-a071283.reason: Barker's displayed g.f. is x^4*(x^19 + ... + x^5 + x^4)/(x^20 - 2x^10 + 1). The numerator polynomial already starts at x^4, so the extra x^4 factor is a transcription typo. The statement deliberately encodes the coefficient list with the doubled factor, so the series starts at x^8. The 'disproof' just observes a(4) = 1 against coefficient 0. I checked that the same g.f. without the extra x^4 reproduces all 80 data terms, and that the second conjunct, a(n) = 2a(n-10) - a(n-20), holds on the data. So the refutation exploits a typo, not the substance of Barker's conjecture, which is evidently correct up to the typo.

oeis-a261387.reason: Sun's conjecture (i) is about n >= 1 (offset 1): a(n) > 0 except for n = 1, 2, 8. The formal statement asserts the equivalence for every n : N, including n = 0, where the right side '0 is not in {1,2,8}' is true but no 0 < k < m with k+m = 0 exists. The 'disproof' uses only this n = 0 case. It says nothing about Sun's conjecture (i) or (ii), which remain open. The mismatch is a domain/offset error in the formalization, and the proof exploits it.

oeis-a293452.reason: The source formula 'T(n,1) = A023855(n)' is off by one. The OEIS data give T(n,1) = 0, 1, 2, 7, 10, 22, ..., while A023855 (offset 1) is 1, 2, 7, 10, 22, ..., so T(n,1) = A023855(n-1). The statement encodes the shifted literal formula, and the disproof just checks width 2 (one toppling against A023855(2) = 2). With n = 1 the inequality says exactly that (1, p^(k+1)-1, p^(k+1)) is an abc-hit, c > rad(abc). The question is therefore an immediate instance of the classical construction of infinitely many abc-hits (a = 1, c a 2-power power of an odd number, with b divisible by a high power of 2; Wikipedia's abc conjecture article gives the 2^(6n) variant). It works for every odd prime. Greg Martin's comment already points out that the k = 1 case is easy. The proof is correct, but the question is answered by a standard textbook argument and was not a genuinely open problem.

oeis-a183761.reason: Kimberling's 2012 conjecture says the count of nonsingular 0..n 2x2 matrices with lexicographically increasing rows equals the count of 0..n matrices with positive determinant. The formal statement encodes this faithfully, with strict lex order on rows and det = ad - bc. The OEIS entry already marks it true. David Radcliffe (Aug 13 2025): 'half of all 2 X 2 nonsingular 0..n matrices have rows in increasing order, and half of them have positive determinant', with a(n) = A062801(n)/2. The Lean proof is exactly Radcliffe's argument: the row swap is an involution that negates the determinant and reverses the row order, and nonsingular matrices have distinct rows. It is correct but already proved in the entry.

oeis-a168670.reason: The formal statement matches the OEIS comment: for n>1 with n%11 in {1,8}, 36n^2+72n+35 is never p(p+2) with p and p+2 both prime. The OEIS entry itself already settles it: the next comment says 'This conjecture is evident' (Bruno Berselli, Jan 07 2013, modified Jul 07 2015). The reason is that 36n^2+72n+35 = (6n+5)(6n+7), which forces p = 6n+5, and 11 divides 6n+5 when n≡1 (mod 11) and divides 6n+7 when n≡8 (mod 11). The proof just replays this argument, so this is not a new result.

oeis-a263450.reason: The formal statement is faithful. a(n) is the least k>0 such that prime(n)^k has a decimal 0, written with Nat.nth Nat.Prime (n-1) for offset 1, and the claim is that a(n)=1 infinitely often. The entry already proves Zak Seidov's conjecture: Robert Israel's comment of Oct 19 2015 notes that by Dirichlet's theorem infinitely many primes are ≡1 (mod 100), and all of them have a(n)=1. The PR formalises this argument from the entry, so it is not new.

oeis-a140472.reason: The statement is faithful: a function satisfying a(0)=0, a(1)=1, a(n)=a(n-a(n-1))+a(floor(n/2)) exists, and every such function equals (n+2^v2(n))/2 for n>0, which is Jon Maiga's 2019 conjecture. The same entry contains a proof. M. F. Hasler (Oct 19-20 2019) shows that A285326/2, characterised by a(2n)=2a(n) and a(2n-1)=n, satisfies the recurrence, and he records the formula a(n)=A285326(n)/2 with 'see comments for the proof'. Hasler's PARI program (n+bitand(n,-n))\2 is the same closed form. The result was proved in 2019, so the PR is not new.

Constant1a.mem_Ico_c1a.reason: The proof certifies C1a ≤ 167952950881157120/111769292050807609 ≈ 1.5026752680 < 1.5028628587. It does this with a 262,144-cell step function, checked by Kronecker substitution and decide +kernel. The Lean argument is sound, and the formal-conjectures definition of C1a is used unchanged. However, the target 1.5028628587 in formal-conjectures is out of date. Tao's optimization-constants page already lists certified constructions below it: EinsteinArena/AgentDiscover at 1.5027435320 (Oct 2026) and Atris at 1.5027434868. More importantly, the file and the PR body say the witness and the Lean bridge are adapted from Will Kirschenman's teorth/optimizationproblems PR #418, which refined Josh Hurst's PR #408. Both of those earlier PRs are Lean-verified and give stronger bounds: Hurst, opened Nov 26 2026, has 1.502664627575, and Kirschenman has 1.502664613439. The merged answer is a quantised copy of their witness that is about 1.1e-5 weaker than either. So this ports and weakens bounds that other people had already proved.

oeis-a082994.reason: The formal statement faithfully encodes the Ogilvy-Anderson claim quoted in A082994: if k > 0, k is not divisible by 10, k != rev(k) and k*rev(k) is a square, then k and rev(k) are both squares. The disproof uses k = 2178 (2178*8712 = 4356^2, and 2178 is not a square). But A082994 is by definition the list of counterexamples to this claim. Its first comment says these numbers 'are counterexamples to the following conjecture', and its data begins 288, 528, ..., 2178, ... The claim was already known to be false in 1957 (Amer. Math. Monthly problem E-1243, linked in the entry). Checking one listed term is not a new result.

oeis-a068689.reason: The statement is faithful. With sandwich d k = 9 d...d 9 (k >= 1 copies of a digit d < 10), primality forces d in {1,2,8}, which is Hilliard's 2005 comment in A068689. The proof is a genuine covering-set argument: modulo 3, 7, 11 and 13 the numbers repeat with period 6 in k (10^6 = 1 and 111111 = 0 modulo each prime), and `decide` checks the residues k mod 6 for every digit outside {1,2,8}. The result is standard and already recorded. Makoto Kamada's near-repdigit tables state 'No prime number of the form 944...449 exists' and 'No prime number of the form 955...559 exists', each with covering set {3,7,11,13}. 977...779 = 11 * 88...89 factors algebraically, which is why Kamada's index has no page for it. Inner digits 0, 3, 6 and 9 are trivially composite, as the entry itself notes. The OEIS 'conjecture' is a well-known covering-congruence fact, not an open problem.

oeis-a000051.reason: The statement formalises the corrected Luschny permanent identity: the permanent of the (n+1)x(n+1) matrix M(j,k) = -floor((j-k-2)/(n+1)) equals 2^n + 1. The statement file itself says 'Sela Fried proved it in Theorem 1 of arXiv:2606.09913'. A000051 records 'The corrected Luschny's conjecture is true (see Fried link). - Sela Fried, Dec 02 2025'. The Lean proof (a recursion W(m+2) = 2W(m+1) on permutation weights) is a valid formalisation of an already-published result. It does not solve an open problem.

arxiv-2003.13166.reason: The formal statement matches Potechin-Tsang Conjecture 1: S is symmetric, does not contain 1 and generates G, and |U| > |G|/2 implies some u in U has at least sqrt(|S|/2) neighbours in U. The disproof is a valid counterexample. In the dihedral group D_9 with S = three reflections {sr0, sr1, sr3}, a 10-element U has induced maximum degree 1, which is less than sqrt(3/2). However, the conjecture was refuted within days of being posed. Lehner and Verret, 'Counterexamples to "A Conjecture on Induced Subgraphs of Cayley Graphs" [arXiv:2003.13166]' (arXiv:2004.01327, April 2020; Ars Math. Contemp.), give several counterexamples. These include an infinite family of Cayley graphs of unbounded valency with an induced subgraph of maximum degree 1 on more than half the vertices. The PR exhibits one more small counterexample to an already-disproved conjecture.

OeisA190969.conjecture_2.reason: The statement is faithful to Sun's conjecture in A190969. It says S(p) = sum_{k<p} a(4k) C(2k,k)^3 / (-4096)^k is 0 mod p^3 for odd primes p = 1, 2, 4 (mod 7), computed in ZMod (p^3); 4096 is invertible there because p is odd. The proof is not original, and its own header says so: 'Ported from the verified Lean proof in Epoch AI's LeanOpenProblems-results, OEIS Open benchmark (T. Adamczewski, arXiv:2608.11941), run oeis-open-lite-gpt6astra, problem oeis_a190969_conjecture_0'. The PR's own work is only a namespace wrapper and the bridge lemmas a_eq/sMod_eq to the catalogue statement. The Epoch results repository shows that run scored C (correct). The supercongruence was therefore already proved and published elsewhere before this PR.

oeis-a053922.reason: The statement says (66...68)^2, with n sixes and n >= 0, has only the digits 2, 4 and 6. This is Dale's 2022 conjecture, faithfully encoded. But A053922 already contains Zhao Hui Du's Mar 11 2024 proof: (66...68)^2 = (4/9)(10^(2n)-1) + (16/9)(10^n-1) + 4 = 44...4 6 22...2 4. The Lean proof formalises exactly that digit pattern (pattern n = 4 :: replicate n 2 ++ 6 :: replicate n 4). Its own docstring says it uses 'Zhao Hui Du's square pattern'. This is an already-proved elementary identity.

oeis-a292728.reason: The formalisation is faithful. A move picks two equal piles x and sends 1 <= y <= x stones between them; an emptied pile is dropped. Terminal states are reachable distinct-part partitions. Both iff conjectures are stated for n >= 1, with truncated subtraction harmless because a(n) <= A000009(n). The proof is genuine: a backward invariant (if every pile after a move is divisible by an odd d, so was every pile before it) makes [n] and pairs of odd parts unreachable; explicit constructions reach every distinct partition when n = 2^k, and every one except [p] when n is an odd prime. However, the substantive directions were already recorded in the companion entry A292727 (unreachable states, same game). There Charlie Neder (Jan 26 2019) gives as formulas, not conjectures, 'a(2^k) = 0' and 'for p an odd prime, a(p) = 1' (and a(2p) = (p+3)/2). These say every state, terminal ones included, is reachable for 2^k, and only [p] is unreachable for odd p. The converse directions follow from the one-line odd-divisor invariant. So both A292728 conjectures were essentially settled in the companion entry, and the PR mostly formalises known facts. Caveat: Neder's formulas carry no written proof in the entry, so this 'known' rests on an OEIS formula claim rather than a published paper.

Erdos1088.erdos_1088.note: The statement (for each fixed n>=3, log2 f_d(n) = o(d), with f_d(n) the least m such that every m-point set in R^d has an n-point subset with distinct distances) is a faithful rendering of erdosproblems.com/1088. However, the proof file says explicitly that it is a port of the public repository H0W4RD-dev/erdos-1088-lean (Howe, Huffman, Kohlmeyer, Kruer, with AI agents). It ports commit d164b38, and all eight commits of that repository are dated 10 Nov 2026, before this PR (27 Nov 2026). That repository already contains a manuscript and a kernel-checked Lean proof of f_d(n) <= n*2^{C_n sqrt(d) log d} against the same formal-conjectures statement. So the result is not new here. Note that it is unrefereed: the repository README says no human expert has reviewed the argument, and erdosproblems.com still lists the problem as open with no proof claim.

Koethe.KotheConjecture.note: The formal statement is faithful. Ideal R in Mathlib is a left ideal, and the claim is that the sum of two nil left ideals is nil; IsNil means every element is nilpotent. The disproof is a genuine ~2100-line construction with no sorry, axioms or native_decide. It builds an algebra over the algebraic closure of Q with a nil two-sided ideal I and an element W of M_2(I) that is not nilpotent, then uses upstream's isNil_iSup_of_kotheConjecture (column ideals) to refute the left-ideal form. But the PR body itself says it follows the nil-ring counterexample of Adamczewski, Bohmler and Marczinzik, 'A counterexample to Kothe's conjecture and a question of Rowen' (arXiv:2609.07996, submitted 7 Sep 2026). So the Kothe conjecture was already refuted in the literature before this PR (27 Nov 2026), and this is a formalization of that published counterexample.

Erdos14.erdos_14.parts.i.note: The statement (for every A and every eps>0, the count of n<=N not uniquely a sum of two elements of A is >> N^{1/2-eps}) matches the first question of erdosproblems.com/14. The problem page now states the problem solved: one always has |[1,N] \ B| >> N^{1/2}, with a link to a formalised proof on conjectures.io. Two conjectures.io proof claims were posted by T. Bloom on 2026-09-27, before this PR (26 Nov 2026). The proof header also attributes the argument to L. Kruer and J. Kohlmeyer's paper 'A uniform square-root lower bound for non-unique sums and a resolution of Erdos problem 14'. So this is a formalization of a known result.

Erdos593.erdos_593.note: The statement asks for the set of finite 3-uniform hypergraphs on Fin n that appear in every 3-uniform hypergraph of chromatic number > aleph_0. The answer given is an explicit classification: after removing isolated vertices, the system is linear, every triple meets a bridge of the incidence (Levi) graph, and all Berge cycles are even. That is a genuine characterization, not a restatement. But it is exactly the classification of Eric Li, 'A Resolution of Erdos Problems 593 and 1177' (arXiv:2606.24882, v1 23 June 2026). Li posted it as a proof claim on erdosproblems.com/593, and the upstream docstring already cites it. The PR openly ports Li's Aristotle Lean development (ericlisg/erdos-593-1177-lean). So this is a formalization of a known (claimed, 2026) result.

Erdos156.erdos_156.note: The statement (the least size of a maximal Sidon subset of [1,N] is O(N^{1/3})) faithfully encodes the Erdos-Sarkozy-Sos question; IsMaximalSidonSetIn means inclusion-maximal within {1..N}. The file and PR say it is a port of the certified conjectures.io result 86a1df7c (solver JenW1N, Lean-verified 2 Nov 2026, certified 6 Nov 2026). That result's review found the statement faithful. erdosproblems.com/156 itself now says that 'a formalised proof that there does exist such a set can be found here', linking to that conjectures.io solution. So this is a re-formalisation of an already-published resolution.

Erdos357.erdos_357.variants.monotone.par.note: The question asks for an explicit g with g = O(h), where h(n) is the longest weakly increasing sequence in [1,n] with distinct consecutive-block sums. The formal statement is trivially satisfiable (answer := 0, as upstream warns). The submitted answer sqrt(n) is the known lower bound: distinct singleton sums force h = f, and erdosproblems.com/357 records f(n) >= (2+o(1)) n^{1/2} (Weisenberg's forum comment, Aug 2025, via Straus's construction for [874]). The file says it is a 'PORT OF A PUBLIC PROOF, not a new result' from KitaKen1's repositories. Nothing about the open growth question is settled.

Green93.green_93.note: irreducibleProb 1 n is the fraction of monic 0/1 polynomials of degree n with constant term 1 that are irreducible, and the claim is that it tends to 1. This is faithfully the Odlyzko-Poonen conjecture as stated in Green's Problem 93. Breuillard-Varju proved it under GRH. Constantin Kogler, 'The Odlyzko-Poonen Conjecture on Irreducibility of Random Polynomials' (arXiv:2609.26771, 22 Sep 2026), states 'We prove the Odlyzko-Poonen conjecture unconditionally' and reports a Lean formalization. The merged proof is adapted from Kogler's ckkogler/odlyzko-poonen-lean, so it formalizes a result already published before this PR.

Koethe.KotherConjecture.variants.two_by_.note: The statement says that for every nil two-sided ideal I of a ring R, M_2(I) is nil. This is a faithful form of the Kothe conjecture, equivalent to it by Krempa, as upstream records. The disproof uses the same construction as PR #6677: a nil ideal I in an explicit algebra over the algebraic closure of Q, and the square of a companion-type matrix with entries in I that is not nilpotent, applied directly via ULift. It is genuine, with no sorry or axioms. The PR states that it follows the counterexample of Adamczewski, Bohmler and Marczinzik (arXiv:2609.07996, 7 Sep 2026), which predates the PR. So this formalizes a published refutation.

Green25.green_25.upper.note: The statement asks for k(N) = o(N/log N) such that Property25 fails, i.e. for a lowering of the Erdos-Sarkozy-Sos upper bound in Green's Problem 25. The answer is k(N) = ceil(N^{23/40}). The pinned formal-conjectures file already contains this exact bound as green_25.variants.upper_pow_23_40, tagged 'research solved'. It records a formal proof at github.com/KitaKen1/green-25-upper-bound (commit 3a54a688, Green25UpperFC.lean), and the merged file is a port of exactly that commit; it even proves the stronger 'eventually fails' form. The PR acknowledges this and says Problem 25 itself is not settled. So this is a formalization of a known result.

Erdos624.erdos_624.note: H(n) is the least m such that some f : P(Fin n) -> Fin n has {f(A) : A subset of Y} = Fin n for every Y with |Y| >= m, and the claim is Tendsto (H n - log2 n) atTop atTop. This faithfully encodes erdosproblems.com/624 (Erdos-Hajnal, with log2 n <= H(n) < log2 n + (3+o(1)) log2 log2 n known). The merged OMA.disproof shows that H(n) - log2 n stays bounded along an unbounded sequence, which refutes the conjecture. But the file and PR say it is a port of the certified conjectures.io result 6f349986 (solver JenW1N, Lean-verified 16 Nov 2026, certified 19 Nov 2026), whose page records that the formal target was not weakened. So the refutation was already public before this PR (27 Nov 2026). It is unrefereed, and erdosproblems.com/624 has no proof claim yet.

Erdos357.erdos_357.variants.monotone.par.note: The question asks for an explicit g with g = o(h). The formal statement is trivially satisfiable (answer := 0). The submitted answer sqrt(n)/log n is strictly weaker than the known lower bound: h = f, and erdosproblems.com/357 records f(n) >= (2+o(1)) n^{1/2} (Weisenberg, via Straus's construction). The file says it is a 'PORT OF A PUBLIC PROOF, not a new result' (KitaKen1), with only the step sqrt(n)/log n = o(sqrt n) added. So nothing open is resolved: the content is a known bound weakened by a log factor.

Erdos1068.erdos_1068.note: The statement asks whether every graph (on a Type) with chromaticCardinal = aleph_1 has a countable induced subgraph that is infinitely connected, meaning nontrivial with infinitely many internally disjoint paths between any two vertices. This is a faithful rendering of the vertex-connectivity question that erdosproblems.com/1068 (and the forum, Jan 2026) says is intended. The disproof is a genuine ZFC construction on labelled tree nodes of height omega_1 (coloured by height; every N-colouring has a conflict), with no sorry. But the file and PR say it is a port of the certified conjectures.io result d5e35e41 (solver JenW1N, Lean-verified 12 Nov 2026, certified 19 Nov 2026). That page records the statement as reviewed and faithful and the countable case as previously open (Soukup 2015, Bowler-Pitz). The resolution was therefore public before this PR (27 Nov 2026), though unrefereed.

PierceBirkhoff.pierce_birkhoff_conjectur.note: The formal statement is faithful. A finite closed semialgebraic cover with f polynomial on each piece forces f to be continuous (pasting lemma), so it is the Henriksen–Isbell piecewise-polynomial notion, and the conclusion is f = sup_i inf_j g_ij with finitely many polynomials. The merged file is a disproof, a 30-dimensional counterexample. Its own header calls it a port of Maxence Faldor's Lean disproof following Lai, Lim and Ren, 'Pierce-Birkhoff conjecture is false' (arXiv:2609.10420, 9 Sep 2026, Theorem 7). So the conjecture was already refuted in the literature (Wikipedia still lists it as open). This is a formalization of a known result.

Koethe.KotherConjecture.variants.general.note: The statement (for every ring R, nil two-sided ideal I and finite n, M_n(I) is nil) is Krempa's equivalent matrix form of the Köthe conjecture, so it is faithful. The disproof builds R = Q·1 + the nil algebra generated by three weighted shifts over a countable field, with a 2x2 matrix W = H^2 in M_2(I) that is not nilpotent. This is the same construction and the same Lean target as the earlier Lean disproof github.com/tadamcz/koethe (GPT-6 Astra/Epoch AI, Sep 2026; that one uses the algebraic closure of F_2, this one the algebraic closure of Q). It is also the construction of Adamczewski–Böhmler–Marczinzik, 'A counterexample to Köthe's conjecture and a question of Rowen' (arXiv:2609.07996, 7 Sep 2026). So it is a genuine refutation, but already published two-plus months before this PR (27 Nov 2026).

Erdos785.erdos_785.variants.chen_conject.note: The statement is Chen's conjecture on erdosproblems.com/785: if A+B contains all large integers and limsup A(x)B(x)/x < 3/2, then A(x)B(x)-x -> infinity. It adds harmless 0 ∉ A, B and infinitude hypotheses, so it is faithful. The proof's header says it follows Zihan Zhang, 'A sharp bound for additive complements' (arXiv:2610.29963, 21 Oct 2026), whose abstract proves exactly this with 3/2 sharp. It was proved independently by van Doorn, Liu and Tang (arXiv:2610.35027, 26 Oct 2026), whose abstract says it confirms Chen's conjecture. So this formalizes a result published a month before the PR.

Erdos963.erdos_963.parts.i.note: The statement f(n) ~ answer(n), with answer = log_2 n, is a faithful reading of 'estimate f(n)' (the order log n is easy, so the constant is the question). It is not a one-sided or trivial bound. But erdosproblems.com/963 itself says that KoishiChan sketched an argument in the comments proving f(n) ~ log_2 n (forum posts of 5 Dec 2025). The file's header says it is a port of Manuel Lopez's public Lean formalization (github.com/jmanuellb/erdos-963-lean) of that argument, 'not a new result'. So this is a known result.

Erdos96.erdos_96.note: The statement (the maximum number of unit distances among n points in convex position is O(n)) is the Erdős–Moser conjecture as stated on the problem page, and the disproof gives, for every k, a strictly convex set where every point has k unit neighbours. erdosproblems.com/96 marks the conjecture false: convex polygons with >> n log log n unit distances exist, and a formalised proof is linked. The file's own attribution says this is an independent formalization of the known refutation by Kruer, Kohlmeyer and Price (Sep 2026), 'not a new discovery'.

Erdos1145.erdos_1145.note: The formal Erdos1145Prop (A, B infinite, nth(A)/nth(B) -> 1, A+B contains all large n ⇒ limsup 1_A*1_B = ∞) is faithful. The upstream version even allows 0, and a counterexample with positive sets refutes both readings. The disproof uses affine blocks at nested coprime scales with bounded representation counts. Its header says it formalizes the counterexample of Howe, Huffman, Kohlmeyer and Kruer, 'Balanced additive complements with bounded representation functions' (hexagonmath 2611.00758, 20–21 Nov 2026), whose abstract gives a negative answer to the Erdős–Sárközy conjecture. That preprint predates this PR (27 Nov 2026), although it is unrefereed and self-labelled as primarily AI-generated. erdosproblems.com/1145 has not been updated (still open).

OeisA179537.conjecture2.note: The statement is faithful: a(n) = Σ C(n,k)^2 C(n-k,k)^2 (-16)^k, and for (p/7) = -1, Σ_{k<p} (-1)^k a(k) ≡ 0 (mod p^2). legendreSym 7 p is (p/7). The OEIS entry does not mark it as proved, but it follows directly from published theorems. Z.-W. Sun, J. Number Theory 132 (2012) (arXiv:1101.1946), Theorem 1.1(i), gives Σ_{k<p} (-1)^k W_k(-x) ≡ Σ_{k<p} C(2k,k)^3 x^k/16^k (mod p^2), where W_n(x) = Σ C(n,k)^2 C(n-k,k)^2 x^k; taking x = 16 turns the sum into Σ C(2k,k)^3. Z.-H. Sun (arXiv:1012.3898, abstract and Theorem 3.2) proved Σ_{k<p} C(2k,k)^3 ≡ 0 (mod p^2) for p ≡ 3,5,6 (mod 7), p > 3, and p = 3 is a direct check (225 ≡ 0 mod 9). The proof is an independent self-contained re-derivation, by the same reduction to Σ C(2k,k)^3 followed by a CM/Hasse-invariant argument, of a result already in the literature.

OeisA79727.conjecture4.note: The statement is faithful to Bala's Conjecture 4 (12 Jul 2024) on OEIS: if n is a product of distinct primes from A003625 (≡ 3,5,6 mod 7), then n^2 divides Σ_{k≤(n-1)/2} C(2k,k)^3. The empty product gives the trivial n = 1 case. The single-prime case is essentially Z.-H. Sun's theorem (arXiv:1012.3898). The squarefree-product statement was already claimed with a written proof and a companion Lean file by Jensen Kohlmeyer and Liam Kruer (manuscript dated 3 Oct 2026, posted publicly in TheJustinSunPrize/awards issue #4912 on 10 Oct 2026), more than a month before this PR. I did not verify that manuscript. The Lean proof here (block reduction plus a Clausen/Gauss hypergeometric argument) is complete, but the result was not new.

Erdos108.erdos_108.note: The formal statement (for all r >= 4, k >= 2 a finite f such that χ(G) >= f gives a subgraph of girth >= r and χ >= k) is Erdős–Hajnal's question as stated. The disproof takes r = 5, k = 5: line graphs of random oriented multipartite graphs that are triangle-free with large χ, and whose C4-free subgraphs are 4-colourable. erdosproblems.com/108 already records the negative answer for r >= 5: triangle-free graphs of arbitrarily large chromatic number all of whose C4-free subgraphs are 3-colourable, with an exposition by Nguyen and Walczak. The file's header says it follows Kohlmeyer–Kruer and Nguyen–Walczak. So it is a formalization of a known disproof.

Erdos1189.erdos_1189.parts.iii.note: maxReciprocalSum(k) =Θ(log k) is a reasonable reading of 'determine or estimate max Σ 1/n_i over irreducible covering sets of size k'. The upper bound H_k is easy; the content is the matching lower construction. But the erdosproblems.com proof-claims page records a claim by Jeff Pickhardt / Omniscience Research Agent (submitted 2026-07-28) that 'the largest reciprocal sum is Θ(log k)', noting that Starfleet's earlier proof also existed. The file's header says the logarithmic order and the prime-block construction were published by Star Fleet Math, crediting earlier work of van Doorn. So the answer log k was already established before this PR; this is a fresh formalization of a known result.

Erdos282.erdos_282.variants.graham.note: The statement faithfully asks whether the greedy algorithm (distinct denominators, per Bloom's clarification in the forum) terminates whenever Graham's representability condition holds for denominators ≡ a (mod d). The disproof is a genuine counterexample: x = 1/119, a = 1, d = 3, where gcd(119, 3) = 1 so x is representable. An explicit 6-step invariant keeps the greedy remainder positive forever. The file's own header says it is a port of Ilia Pauzner's counterexample, which already exists as a Lean disproof (credited 'using Gemini') in his public formal-conjectures fork. So the result is not original to this PR. Pauzner's counterexample is unpublished and not on erdosproblems.com, and I could not establish its date beyond the cited commit.

Green31.green_31.upper.note: The formal statement asks for F(N) <= answer(N) infinitely often, with answer(N) <= sqrt(N) + c N^{1/4} + C for some c < 0.94349 (Hou–Zhao, arXiv:2607.01169). The proof gives F(N) <= sqrt(N) + 0.9434 N^{1/4} for all N >= 10^24, by a new 13-kernel certificate for Hou–Zhao's smoothing method. That is valid but improves 0.94349 only to 0.9434. A stronger bound was already published: Carter, O'Bryant and Tao, 'On the diameter and distribution of Sidon sets' (arXiv:2610.36207, 26 Oct 2026), Corollary 1.2, give |A| <= N^{1/2} + 0.94304 N^{1/4} + 0.44466 for Sidon A ⊆ [1,N] with |A| >= 483. Together with the trivial case |A| < 483, this already satisfies the formal statement with c = 0.94304. The upstream reference to HZ26 as the record is out of date, so the improvement asked for was already known.

Green35.green_35.lower.note: The formal 'lower' statement only asks for a valid lower bound for c(p) that beats sqrt(4/7) ≈ 0.75593 at p = 2 (or 0.64 at p = ∞). That is a variant of Green's 'estimate c_p'. The proof gives c(2) >= 473/625 = 0.7568 by a polynomial-kernel Fourier argument, and sets the answer to 0 at every p ≠ 2. A better bound was in the literature long before. E. P. White, 'An almost-tight L^2 autoconvolution inequality' (arXiv:2210.16437, 2022), Theorem 1, proves 0.574635728 <= inf ||f*f||_2^2 for real-valued f on a unit interval with ∫f = 1, i.e. c(2) >= 0.75805; restricting to nonnegative f only raises the infimum. White also cites Martin–O'Bryant's earlier 0.574575 (c(2) >= 0.75801). Both exceed 0.7568, so 'improving sqrt(4/7)' was already done (the upstream docstring is out of date), and this bound is weaker than the known one.

Erdos878.erdos_878.parts.v.note: The statement H ~ answer is an answer-style question, and the proof supplies the explicit equivalent H(x) ~ x * sum_{p <= (log x)^2} e^{-r_p(x)}/p * (r_p(x) + log p/(p-1)), where r_p(x) = log x - floor(log_p x) log p, proved with a Selberg-sieve tail bound. As an asymptotic formula this is a substantive, non-tautological answer to Erdős's 'find an asymptotic formula for H(x)'. However, the file's own header says it is a single-file port of rivkalipko/erdos-878-asymptotics (Rivka Lipkovitz with OpenAI Codex, PALOMAR-2026-11-19), a public Lean proof of exactly this formula that predates the 2026-11-27 merge. erdosproblems.com/878 has not been updated (0 proof claims, and no forum comment on part (v)). So this re-formalises an already-public result rather than giving a new one.

Erdos1032.erdos_1032.note: The formal statement is faithful: there exist c>0 and infinitely many n with a 4-critical graph (vertex- and edge-critical, chromatic number 4) on Fin n of minimum degree >= cn. The extra vertex-criticality is harmless because positive minimum degree excludes isolated vertices. The disproof shows every such graph has minimum degree o(n), using a bounded-depth list-colouring branching plus 2-SAT certificates whose union has linearly many edges, and edge-criticality then forces all edges into the union. The file's header says it formalises EthanYang's sparse-obstruction argument. That disproof was Lean-verified and approved on conjectures.io (verified 24 Oct 2026, certified 28 Oct 2026), before this 2026-11-27 merge. erdosproblems.com/1032 still lists the problem as open with 0 proof claims, but the result was already public, so this is a re-formalisation.

Koethe.KotherConjecture.variants.le_Koth.note: The statement (every nil left ideal lies in the Köthe radical, the sum of all nil two-sided ideals) is a standard equivalent of Köthe's conjecture and is formalised faithfully (Ideal R = left ideal; IsNil = all elements nilpotent). The disproof builds a ring (a unital subring of a banded incidence algebra over the algebraic closure of Q, generated by three weighted shifts) with a nil two-sided ideal I such that a 2x2 companion-square matrix over I is not nilpotent. This is Krempa's matrix form, and the proof passes to the le_KotherRadical form through the upstream column-ideal lemmas. It contains no sorry or axioms. But Köthe's conjecture was already refuted in September 2026: Adamczewski-Böhmler-Marczinzik, arXiv:2609.07996 (7 Sep 2026), plus the GPT-6 Astra Lean disproof of the same Krempa matrix form (tadamcz/koethe), which uses a very similar shift-operator/pencil/common-zero construction. So this is a formalisation of a known result.

OeisA114216.conjecture.note: The formal statement 'a(n) != 1 for all n > 33900' is a faithful reading of OEIS A114216's question 'Is a(33900) the last term equal to 1?', and the recurrence matches OEIS (a(n) is the odd part of a(n-1)+prime(n)). The disproof kernel-checks a(78493252) = 1 (567791839 + 1579691809 = 2^31) using a wheel sieve with decide +kernel and no native_decide. That counterexample was already found by Donovan Johnson in May 2010 and is recorded in OEIS A114217 (term 78493252) and A114218 (k=31), as the proof header itself says. The A114216 comment is simply stale, so this formalises a known result.

Green31.green_31.variants.upper_eventual.note: The statement asks for a bound F(N) <= answer(N) for all large N, with answer(N) - sqrt N <= c N^{1/4} + C for some c < 0.94349 (the Hou-Zhao constant). This faithfully encodes 'improve the [HZ26] upper bound', but that is a moving record, not Green's original threshold. The proof gives c = 0.9434 via an explicit 13-component certificate (sqrt(ab) ≈ 0.94335) inside Hou-Zhao's vector-valued smoothing framework, and appears sound (decide +kernel, no native_decide). However, smaller constants in the same framework were posted publicly before the 2026-11-27 merge, on the erdosproblems.com #30 forum: 0.94325 (JoshMadeiros, 17 Aug 2026, with Lean-checked covering inequalities) and 0.9428096 (johnakwei, 5 Oct 2026, which also argues 2*sqrt(2)/3 is the method's limit). Both are unrefereed, but they already beat 0.94349 by more than this proof does. This is a weaker re-derivation of an already-achieved improvement.

Erdos36.erdos_36.variants.upper.note: The formal statement asks for limsup M(N)/N <= c with c < 0.380926853433087, which is Haugland's old bound. erdosproblems.com/36 records that this was already beaten: the current record is c < 0.380876 (TTT-Discover, 2026), improving on AlphaEvolve [GGTW25] and Haugland. The proof establishes limsup <= 0.3809, using a 512-bin step function block-averaged from the atrislabs/records construction plus a probabilistic rounding argument. That is valid but weaker than the published record. The catalogue threshold is stale, so this proves an already-known (indeed already-improved) bound.

Erdos1063.erdos_1063.better_upper.note: The statement asks for an answer g with n_k = O(g) and g = o(k * lcm(1..k-1)), improving Cambie's bound; this is a reasonable reading of 'estimate n_k'. The proof gives g(k) = exp(k/log k * (log log k + log log log k + log 2)). The upstream formal-conjectures file itself records exactly this bound as research solved (erdos_1063.variants.subexponential_upper_bound), formally proved by the LEAP agent (lfsong-google fork, commit ff33e501). The OMA file's header says it is adapted from that proof, and it uses the same folded-pigeonhole/Chebyshev construction (n_le_folded_pigeonhole_product appears verbatim in the source). So this is a port of a known formal result.

Erdos357.erdos_357.parts.ii.bigO_version.note: This is an answer-style variant: find g with g = O(f), where f(n) is the largest increasing sequence in [1,n] with distinct consecutive-block sums. The proof takes g = sqrt n. That is exactly the order of Weisenberg's known lower bound f(n) >= (2+o(1)) sqrt n, cited on erdosproblems.com/357 and recorded upstream as solved (erdos_357.variants.weisenberg). The file declares itself a 'PORT OF A PUBLIC PROOF, not a new result' (KitaKen1/erdos-357-sqrt-lower-bound). The upstream note itself warns that such answer variants admit easy solutions, and this one adds nothing on how f grows (whether f(n) = o(n) is still open).

Green77.green_77.note: The statement 'exists o -> 0 with alpha(n) << n^{-2+o(n)}', where alpha(n) is the Heilbronn sup-min triangle area in the unit disc (Erdos507.alpha), faithfully encodes Green's question of whether there is always a triangle of area at most n^{-2+o(1)}. The disproof gives arbitrarily large n-point sets with every triangle of area >= n^{-2+eta} for a fixed eta > 0, then translates them into the disc. The file states it is a port of OpenAI's openai/math Lean development (OAI.Problem355.heilbronn_power_lower_bound, family 191, 'A power improvement in the Heilbronn triangle lower bound'), whose preprint is dated September 2026. So the power-saving lower bound refuting Green 77 was already public before this 2026-11-27 merge.

Erdos357.erdos_357.parts.ii.littleO_vers.note: This is an answer-style variant: find g with g = o(f). The proof takes g = sqrt n / log n and combines the known sqrt n = O(f) (Weisenberg's f(n) >= (2+o(1)) sqrt n, on erdosproblems.com/357 and solved upstream) with the trivial sqrt n / log n = o(sqrt n). The file declares itself a port of a public proof (KitaKen1/erdos-357-sqrt-lower-bound). It is strictly weaker than the bigO variant and gives no new information about the growth of f, so it is a formalisation of a known result.

Erdos143.erdos_143.parts.ii.note: The statement says every well-separated A in (1, inf) (|kx - y| >= 1 for distinct x, y and k >= 1) has sum 1/(x log x) < inf, which is faithful to Erdős's first question. The proof disproves it with an explicit countable set of rationals in [2, inf) whose weight diverges, and checks that the set meets all the WellSeparatedSet hypotheses. The file states it is a port of Mattia Apicella's Lean development (mapice/erdos-143-candidate-disproof, commit 0f4b969). erdosproblems.com/143 already links that commit as 'a formalised negative answer to the first question', and the catalogue's erdosState is 'solved'. So this formalises a known result.

Erdos14.erdos_14.parts.ii.note: The statement 'there exists A with |[1,N] \ B| = o(sqrt N)', where B is the set of integers with exactly one representation as a sum of two elements of A, faithfully encodes Erdős's second question. The proof shows that every A has at least sqrt(N)/12000 non-uniquely represented integers for large N. The file says the argument and helper lemmas are adapted from L. Kruer and J. Kohlmeyer (liamkruer.com, Erdos14_PartII_Counterexample.lean). erdosproblems.com/14 already states that the answer to the second question is no (|[1,N] \ B| >> N^{1/2}) and links a formalised proof, and the catalogue's erdosState is 'solved'. So this is a known result.

MeanValueProblem.mean_value_problem.note: The statement is Smale's mean value conjecture with K = 1 (the K argument is unused). It says that for deg p >= 2 and any z there is a critical point c with |p(z)-p(c)|/|z-c| <= |p'(z)|, which is faithful; Lean's x/0 = 0 convention only makes the claim easier. The proof refutes it with a large-degree polynomial approximating a model built on the cubic lemniscate |(z^3+36i)/sqrt 1297| <= 1. But the K = 1 conjecture was already disproved in September 2026: a GPT-6 Astra Lean disproof against the same formal-conjectures statement (tadamcz/mean-value-problem, a quartic four-petal version of the same normal-re-entry idea), explained in Adamczewski-Colbrook, arXiv:2610.36158 (26 Oct 2026), which gives an explicit degree-29,984 example. This proof uses a different lemniscate but proves a known result.

Koethe.KotherConjecture.variants.matrixO.note: The statement Nil*(M_n(R)) = M_n(Nil*(R)) for every finite index type n is a standard equivalent (Krempa) of Köthe's conjecture and is formalised faithfully. The proof file is identical to the le_KotherRadical disproof except for the final bridge: it reuses the same ring with a nil ideal I and a non-nilpotent W in M_2(I), and deduces a contradiction via isNil_kotheRadical and the ULift(Fin 2) reindexing. Köthe's conjecture, in exactly this matrix form, was already refuted in September 2026: Adamczewski-Böhmler-Marczinzik, arXiv:2609.07996, and the GPT-6 Astra Lean disproof of KotherConjecture.variants.general_matrix (tadamcz/koethe). So this is a formalisation of a known result.

Erdos161.erdos_161.parts.ii.note: The statement says that for t >= 3 and all alpha, beta in (0, 1/2), F^{(t)}(n, alpha) = Theta(F^{(t)}(n, beta)), using balancedColoringThreshold. This faithfully encodes 'for fixed t >= 3, do all positive densities below 1/2 give the same asymptotic order?' (the 'one jump at 0' guess). The proof file itself says the result is Corollary 3 of Dhruv Mubayi, 'Large blow-ups of uniform hypergraphs', arXiv:2611.33108 (posted 24 Nov 2026), and it formalises Mubayi's blow-up theorem. Mubayi's abstract gives the order (log n)^{1/(k-1)} for every fixed 0 < alpha < 1/2 and refers to Erdős's $500 question. The t=3 case was already Conlon-Fox-Sudakov 2011. The published solution predates the 2026-11-27 merge, so this is a formalisation of a known result (the erdosproblems page is not yet updated).

opg-inverse-of-an-integer-matrix.reason: The source asks when [D X] (D diagonal with entries >= 2) has an integer right inverse; the poster guesses 'the integers in each row need to be relatively prime'. The statement turns this guess into an iff, and the disproof uses d=(2,2), X=[[1,0],[1,0]]: two equal primitive rows, so no right inverse. That is trivial. The question itself is classical: an integer m x N matrix has an integer right inverse iff the gcd of its m x m minors is 1, equivalently its Smith normal form is [I 0]. Also, 'need' can be read as necessity only, which is trivially true, so the iff reading strengthens the guess. Nothing open was resolved.

opg-vertex-coloring-of-graph-fractional-.reason: Iradmusa's conjecture (chi(G^{m/n}) = omega(G^{m/n}) for connected G with Delta >= 3 and 1 < m < n) was already disproved by Hartke, Liu and Petříčková, 'On coloring of fractional powers of graphs', arXiv:1212.3898 (2012). They give a graph H with chi(H^{3/5}) > omega(H^{3/5}) and show the conjecture holds for even m. The PR's counterexample, the triangular prism, is a new instance, but the conjecture was refuted more than a decade earlier; the OPG page was not updated.

oeis-a216440.reason: Kiolein's conjecture: the number of in-shuffles that reverse 2(n-1) cards is the least m with 2n-1 | 2^m+1. oeis-a213510.reason: Irvine's conjecture is that Cha's N(n) is the partial sums of A064099. In Cha's paper N(n) = sumd(N_3(n)), the sum of inclusive depths of a null-balanced ternary tree, which the BFS complete-tree formalization models faithfully. The n-th node's depth is the tree height, ceil(log_3(2n+1)) by Cha's Fact 1 (eq. 10), which is exactly A064099(n-1). So the conjecture is an immediate consequence of the cited source.

oeis-a286666.reason: The statement (a(n)/n -> 1+sqrt(2) for the positions of 0 in the {0->01}-transform of the Pell word) is faithful. The entry itself says: 'This conjecture follows easily from the fact that (a(n)) is a Beatty sequence, see my comments in A286665. - Michel Dekking, Mar 11 2018', and A286665 gives the Beatty formula with alpha = 2-sqrt(2). The statement file quotes this. Settled in 2018.

oeis-a286015.reason: The conjecture that A286015 (the sum of the largest parts of partitions into consecutive parts) is the row sums of A286013 is stated faithfully, with A286013 defined from its name. In A286013, Peter Munn (Jun 2017) proved Conjecture 1: each nonzero T(n,k) is the largest part of the partition of n into k consecutive parts. Summing over k gives this conjecture (Conjecture 2 there) at once. The Lean proof is just that termwise identity, so the result is essentially definitional and was already settled.

oeis-a287614.reason: Gerasimov's conjecture: if x>=1 and (1+x)^y+(-x)^y is an odd prime, then y is an odd prime or 2^k with k>=1. The statement reads it faithfully. The same author states the same conjecture in A285929, where Jeppe Stig Nielsen (Feb 2023) notes that it can be proved by the algebraic factorizations. It is the classical fact that a^y - b^y prime forces y prime, and that a^y + b^y prime forces y to be a power of 2. The Lean proof is exactly that argument.

oeis-a326578.reason: If n is Carmichael then n | D_{n-1}, the denominator of B_{n-1} (Pomerance-Selfridge-Wagstaff, Math.
